name: 1960 Election Stolen for Kennedy
summary: Claims that Richard Nixon actually won the 1960 U.S. presidential election but lost to John F. Kennedy only because of voter fraud orchestrated by Chicago's Democratic political machine under Mayor Richard J. Daley, plus irregularities in Texas. The theory rests largely on a 1960s newspaper series by journalist Earl Mazo; recounts and later historical analysis found no fraud large enough to have changed the outcome.
evidence_for: Earl Mazo's 1960 New York Herald Tribune series alleged widespread voting irregularities in Cook County, Illinois and in Texas
Individual precincts were found where Nixon votes had been undercounted
Kennedy's narrow margins in Illinois and Texas fed suspicion given Mayor Daley's political-machine reputation
Historian Paul Johnson's 1997 book A History of the American People repeated the claim that Eisenhower urged Nixon to contest the results
evidence_against: Republican-requested recounts found undercounts benefiting both candidates, none large enough to flip the result
Kennedy's strong Cook County performance is explained by the county's large Black and Catholic population, both heavily pro-Kennedy demographics that year
The Texas 'more votes than registered voters' claim ignores that veterans and the elderly were exempt from the era's poll-tax registration requirement
The only state that changed after recount was Hawaii, which flipped to Kennedy, not Nixon
A journalist close to Eisenhower said this was the first time he ever caught Nixon in a lie, regarding the claim Eisenhower urged a legal challenge

sources.title: 1960 U.S. presidential election conspiracy theories — RationalWiki

research_note: RationalWiki article itself cites Slate/Salon (David Greenberg, 'Was Nixon Robbed?') as its main source; that URL was not independently fetched this session so is not listed separately.

name: 2004 U.S. Presidential Election Fraud Theory
summary: Following George W. Bush's narrow 2004 win over John Kerry, decided by Ohio's 20 electoral votes, some conspiracy theorists — most prominently Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in a 2006 Rolling Stone article — alleged the election was stolen through voter suppression, faulty voting-machine allocation, and manipulated exit polls. Investigations attributed the discrepancies to bureaucratic problems and known exit-poll sampling bias rather than coordinated fraud.
evidence_for: Ohio Secretary of State Kenneth Blackwell, a Republican, purged roughly 300,000 voters and oversaw an allocation of voting machines that left predominantly Black, Democratic-leaning precincts with long lines.
Early exit polls showed Kerry leading in enough battleground states to win, before the certified vote count reversed that.
RFK Jr.'s 2006 Rolling Stone article compiled numerous Ohio-county irregularities into a single narrative of systematic rigging.
evidence_against: Ohio's voter purge followed a codified state law requiring removal of inactive voters, not an ad hoc partisan scheme.
The Democratic Party's own post-election report found provisional-ballot rates were nearly identical for Kerry and Bush voters (4.2% vs 4.1%), contradicting claims of disproportionate suppression.
Mitofsky International, which conducted the exit polls, attributed the pro-Kerry skew to Kerry voters being more willing to participate in exit polling, a documented bias, not vote manipulation.
A Salon critique (Farhad Manjoo) noted Ohio's bipartisan local election boards would have required Democratic collusion for a Republican-only rigging scheme to succeed.
research_note: RW article's 'Conspiracy theories' section (citing RFK Jr.'s 2006 Rolling Stone piece and its critics) is the only source seen this session.

name: 440 Hz Music Tuning Conspiracy
summary: Promoted largely by Leonard Horowitz and various New Age and conspiracy websites, this claim holds that the standard A440 Hz musical tuning pitch was imposed, allegedly by Nazi propagandists and later international standards bodies, to disrupt humanity's 'natural' cosmic resonance, and that reverting to A432 Hz or 'solfeggio frequencies' can heal the body and mind.
evidence_for: Historical variability in tuning standards existed before wide adoption of A440 in the 20th century.
432 is a composite number that produces round-number harmonics in some just-intonation calculations, cited by proponents as evidence of cosmic significance.
evidence_against: No credible historical documentation connects Nazi Germany to the international adoption of A440, which was standardized by the ISO in 1955 for practical acoustic and manufacturing reasons.
Claims that A432 heals DNA or the body rely on pseudoscientific misuse of terms like 'frequency' and 'resonance' with no controlled clinical evidence.
Human perception of absolute pitch is culturally and individually variable; there is no evidence of an innate biological preference for any specific tuning standard.
The 'solfeggio frequencies' promoted alongside A432 are a modern invention with no basis in historical solfège music theory.

name: Abortion as Black Genocide
summary: This theory holds that legal abortion (and, in some tellings, birth control and past forced-sterilization programs) functions as a deliberate, if often unstated, eugenic campaign to reduce the Black population, citing the higher abortion rate among Black women and Planned Parenthood founder Margaret Sanger's eugenicist advocacy. Proponents span both Black nationalist groups, such as the Nation of Islam, and White anti-abortion activists.
evidence_for: Black women in the US have a disproportionately higher abortion rate than white women
Planned Parenthood founder Margaret Sanger publicly supported eugenics, though she framed it as voluntary and opposed racial targeting
Real historical anti-Black population-control programs existed, including coerced sterilizations that continued into the 1970s
evidence_against: The US Black population has grown continuously throughout the era of legal abortion, contradicting a 'genocide' framing
Modern Planned Parenthood does not endorse eugenics and disavows Sanger's historical views on the subject
Higher abortion rates among Black women correlate with documented socioeconomic disparities in healthcare and contraception access, not a coordinated extermination plan
No internal document or credible whistleblower account links clinic siting or funding decisions to a population-reduction goal

name: ACORN Voter Fraud Conspiracy
summary: Conservative activists and Tea Party figures alleged that the community organizing group ACORN engineered widespread voter fraud to install Barack Obama as president, and separately that it used a 'Cloward-Piven strategy' to force banks into bad loans that caused the 2008 financial crisis.
evidence_for: James O'Keefe's 2009 undercover videos of ACORN employees appearing to give advice on illegal activity
John McCain's 2008 campaign ran ads claiming ACORN engaged in 'widespread voter fraud'
A few ACORN employees were confirmed to have falsified voter registration forms to get paid for work they hadn't done
evidence_against: An FBI investigation found no evidence of widespread voter fraud, only isolated registration-form falsification by underpaid canvassers
The O'Keefe videos were found to be selectively edited and partially fabricated
FactCheck.org and PolitiFact rated the 'ACORN stole the election' and banking-crisis claims false
ACORN disbanded in 2010 after funding was pulled amid the controversy, well before any of the alleged schemes could be substantiated
research_note: RationalWiki's ACORN article catalogs the 2008-2010 conspiracy theories (voter fraud, Cloward-Piven/banking-crisis engineering, Obama-puppet, black-uprising/FEMA-camp claims) surrounding the now-defunct organization; not present in the atlas under any other id.

name: Adrenochrome Harvesting
summary: QAnon-adjacent believers claim a global elite tortures and murders children to harvest adrenochrome, a naturally occurring chemical, believing it functions as a life-extending drug obtainable only from terrified living victims.
evidence_for: Adrenochrome is a real chemical produced by oxidation of adrenaline, lending the myth a veneer of scientific plausibility
Fictional depictions in works by Hunter S. Thompson and Aldous Huxley are cited by believers as if they were factual accounts
The 2018 YourNewsWire 'Frazzledrip' article claiming a Clinton 'snuff film' spread widely on social media and seeded the modern version of the theory
evidence_against: Adrenochrome is trivially synthesized in a lab and sold commercially by chemical suppliers, eliminating any need to extract it from victims
No law-enforcement investigation has ever found evidence of an adrenochrome-harvesting operation
Human trials found adrenochrome produces no hallucinations, only a severe headache, contradicting the 'miracle drug' claim

name: Alien Abduction Phenomenon
summary: Since the 1960s, thousands of people have reported being taken aboard alien spacecraft, subjected to physical examinations, and returned with periods of unexplained missing time. Mainstream researchers attribute these accounts to sleep paralysis, hypnotic confabulation, and cultural scripts drawn from science fiction rather than genuine extraterrestrial contact.
evidence_for: Consistent narrative structure (capture, examination, conference, return) reported across thousands of independent accounts
Some abductees pass polygraph tests and show genuine psychological distress consistent with real trauma
A small number of physical marks or 'implants' have been offered by believers as corroborating physical evidence
evidence_against: Sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucination fully account for the paralysis/bright-light/missing-time pattern common to accounts
Hypnotic regression, the technique used to 'recover' most abduction memories, is known to produce false memories through suggestion
Alleged 'alien implants' examined by qualified professionals have turned out to be ordinary glass or grit lodged in tissue
The reported alien physiology and motives shift with contemporary popular culture (fairies and demons historically, then 'grey aliens' after The X-Files)

name: Armenian Genocide Denial
summary: Armenian genocide denial is the persistent claim, propagated primarily by the Turkish state and Turkish nationalists since the 1920s, that the Ottoman Empire's 1915-1918 mass killing and deportation of Armenians, Greeks, and Assyrians was not a deliberate genocide but wartime relocation, disease, and mutual ethnic violence.
evidence_for: Turkish denialists attribute Armenian civilian deaths to wartime relocation and disease rather than intentional extermination
Some point to Armenian resistance and collaboration with Russian forces as provoking retaliatory violence
Turkey disputes the death-toll figures commonly cited by historians
evidence_against: Direct telegrams from Ottoman officials including Talaat Pasha explicitly order extermination ('Burn-Destroy-Kill')
Contemporary diplomatic records from Britain, France, Russia, Germany, and the US document mass killings in real time
Deportation marches were systematically conducted without food, water, or medical care, resulting in mass death by design
43 countries and numerous historians' associations formally recognize the events as genocide

name: Aurora Black-Project Aircraft
summary: Aurora is the popular name for an alleged secret US hypersonic reconnaissance aircraft, supposedly developed to replace the SR-71 Blackbird and linked to unexplained sonic booms over California and Nevada in the early 1990s. The US government has never confirmed such a plane existed, and former Lockheed Skunk Works director Ben Rich stated 'Aurora' was merely a budget code name later tied to the B-2 bomber program.
evidence_for: The word 'Aurora' appeared in a 1985 US budget document under a redacted 'black aircraft production' line item
Unexplained sonic booms and unusual pulsing contrails were recorded over the American Southwest in the early 1990s
The US military is known to run classified 'black' aerospace programs, such as the F-117 stealth fighter and X-37B space plane
evidence_against: Former Lockheed Skunk Works director Ben Rich said 'Aurora' referred to a budget line for the B-2 stealth-bomber fly-off, not a hypersonic plane
No wreckage, defector testimony, or verified photograph of an actual Aurora aircraft has ever surfaced
The purported sonic booms and contrails are also produced by conventional aircraft and munitions tests
Lockheed's own proposed hypersonic successor, the SR-72, was not publicly floated until 2007, decades after the 'Aurora' rumors began

name: Satanic Backmasking in Rock Music
summary: A moral panic originating with Christian evangelists in the early 1980s claimed that rock musicians deliberately embedded backward ('backmasked') messages promoting Satanism, drug use, or the occult into their songs, discernible only when the record was played in reverse.
evidence_for: Christian evangelists such as Jacob Aranza and Gary Greenwald played reversed tracks to audiences claiming to hear satanic phrases
The Peters Brothers held 'anti-rock crusades' presenting backward-audio examples as proof
Some proponents argued the brain could subconsciously register backward speech as a form of subliminal messaging
evidence_against: Acoustic analysis shows the alleged messages are artifacts of ordinary forward vocals that coincidentally resemble other phrases when reversed, not deliberately recorded backward content
No band or engineer has ever been shown to have intentionally recorded backward satanic messages
The panic was one strand of the broader, unsubstantiated Satanic Panic of the 1980s
research_note: RW article covers the 1980s evangelical backmasking scare specifically; distinct from the general 'satanic messages in music' genre-wide claims already covered by memphis-rap.

name: Beale Ciphers Treasure
summary: The Beale ciphers are three coded messages from an 1885 pamphlet claiming to describe a vast buried treasure in Bedford County, Virginia, left in the 1820s by a mysterious prospector named Thomas Beale. Only one of the three ciphers has ever been solved, and over a century of searching has turned up no verifiable trace of Beale or the treasure.
evidence_for: One of the three ciphers was successfully decoded using the US Declaration of Independence as a key, yielding a description of the treasure's supposed contents
The pamphlet's narrative detail (dated letters, named innkeeper) gave early readers reason to think it plausible
Hundreds of treasure hunters have searched Bedford County over more than a century, sustaining continued interest in the story
evidence_against: No third-party historical record confirms Thomas Beale or his alleged 30-person mining party ever existed
The pamphlet quotes 1820s letters using words ('stampede', 'improvise') not attested in English until decades later
Cryptographers found the two still-unsolved ciphers show statistical characteristics inconsistent with genuine encoded English text
Stylistic analysis suggests one author wrote the supposed words of all three men (Beale, the innkeeper Morriss, and the anonymous pamphleteer), implying fabrication

name: Benghazi Attack Conspiracy Theories
summary: A cluster of conspiracy theories surrounding the September 11, 2012 attack on the US consulate in Benghazi, Libya, alleging that the Obama administration ordered military support to 'stand down,' deliberately misled the public by blaming a YouTube video, and covered up the truth to protect Hillary Clinton politically.
evidence_for: Early administration statements inconsistently attributed the attack to protests over an anti-Islam video rather than premeditated terrorism
Rep. Jason Chaffetz claimed rescue teams were told to 'stand down' rather than respond
A CBS '60 Minutes' report in 2013 aired a security contractor's dramatic stand-down account
Eight congressional investigations were launched, which proponents cited as evidence something was being hidden
evidence_against: Eight separate congressional investigations, plus reports by the Park Police, State Department, and a 2013 New York Times investigation, found no stand-down order and no evidence of a cover-up
The 'stand-down' rescue teams were contacted only after the attack had already occurred, so they could not have responded in time regardless
CBS retracted its '60 Minutes' report after finding its source, Dylan Davies, was not at the scene and had given contradictory accounts to the FBI
The claim Clinton 'slept through' a 3am alert call is contradicted by witnesses placing her at her office and by the actual attack time (9:30pm EST, not 3am)

name: Bermeja Island CIA Destruction Theory
summary: A Mexican conspiracy theory holding that the CIA covertly destroyed, e.g. by dynamiting, the small Gulf of Mexico island of Bermeja in the 1970s in order to shift the Mexico-U.S. maritime border and give the United States a larger share of oil-rich Gulf of Mexico waters.
evidence_for: Bermeja appeared on maps from the 17th century onward but has not been sighted or photographed since the 19th century, and a 1997 Mexican naval survey failed to locate it.

The island's presence or absence has real legal consequences for the Mexico-U.S. maritime boundary and oil rights in the Gulf of Mexico, a motive some Mexican politicians and media have found suspicious.
evidence_against: The Mexican government's own assessment attributes the island's disappearance to natural causes such as sea-level rise or tectonic subsidence, not sabotage.
The area where Bermeja was charted has since been surveyed at roughly 40 meters depth with no trace of a former landmass consistent with recent destruction.

A president of Mexico's Society of Geography has suggested Bermeja may have been a deliberately fictitious map entry from the start, inserted to mislead rival mapmakers, rather than a real island later destroyed.
No physical, satellite, or documentary evidence of a CIA demolition operation has ever been produced.

name: Black Helicopters
summary: In the early-1990s US militia movement, unmarked black helicopters sighted over military bases and rural areas were claimed to be preparing a covert United Nations/New World Order military occupation of the United States. The claim became so implausible that the term later took on a life of its own as an ironic byword for baseless conspiracy theorizing.
evidence_for: Unmarked black or dark-green helicopters have genuinely been photographed and filmed over US military bases and rural areas since the early 1990s.

The US military does operate real classified stealth helicopters, such as the modified UH-60 Black Hawks used in the 2011 raid that killed Osama bin Laden, lending superficial plausibility to 'secret helicopter' claims.
evidence_against: No UN or federal invasion force, martial-law declaration, or occupation plan has ever materialized despite over 30 years of the claim circulating.
Sightings are readily explained by routine military, medical, news, and law-enforcement helicopter traffic.
The core claims trace to two 1993-94 VHS documentaries (Linda Thompson's 'America Under Siege' and Mark Koernke's 'America in Peril') that mixed genuine footage with unsupported speculation.

name: CDC Whistleblower / MMR-Autism Cover-up
summary: Anti-vaccine activists allege that CDC scientist William Thompson's 2014 recorded admission that a 2004 study omitted a subgroup finding proves the agency covered up evidence that the MMR vaccine causes autism in African-American boys. The claim became a central anti-vaccination-movement narrative and inspired the 2016 film 'Vaxxed'.
evidence_for: William Thompson, a co-author of the 2004 DeStefano et al. study, admitted in secretly recorded phone calls that statistically significant data on African-American boys had been omitted from the published paper.
The controversy prompted a congressional representative to publicly call for an investigation into the alleged cover-up.
evidence_against: Numerous large-scale studies before and after 2004 have found no causal link between the MMR vaccine and autism in any population.
Brian Hooker's 'reanalysis' of the omitted data, which fueled the controversy, was retracted by its journal for undisclosed conflicts of interest and flawed statistical methods.
The CDC had already published public instructions for accessing the underlying 2004 data years before the 'whistleblower' story broke, undercutting the cover-up narrative.

name: Cholesterol/Statin "Lie" (Lipid Hypothesis Denial)
summary: Promoted by figures like former cardiac surgeon Dwight Lundell and other low-carb/high-fat diet advocates, this theory holds that high cholesterol and LDL levels do not meaningfully cause heart disease, and that mainstream medicine — aided by the pharmaceutical industry — has manufactured and maintained a 'cholesterol lie' since 1948 to sell statins and low-fat diets.
evidence_for: Lundell cites decades of clinical experience performing over 5,000 cardiac surgeries as the basis for rejecting the mainstream lipid hypothesis.
Proponents point to individual patients with high LDL and no heart disease as apparent counterexamples to the cholesterol-heart disease link.
Genuine open scientific questions about inflammation's role in atherosclerosis are cited by proponents as partial validation.
A 2016 Kendrick-coauthored systematic review found no clear association between LDL cholesterol and mortality in elderly populations in the studies it examined.
Statins do carry real, sometimes underreported side effects that fuel skepticism of blanket prescribing guidelines.
evidence_against: Decades of large-scale epidemiological and interventional trials consistently show that lowering LDL cholesterol reduces cardiovascular events.
Lundell lost his Arizona medical license in 2008 for professional misconduct and negligence, undermining his claimed authority on the subject.
Quackwatch and the National Council Against Health Fraud both state Lundell's claims contradict the weight of cardiology research.
No peer-reviewed research supports the claim that removing carbohydrates from the diet cures or prevents heart disease.

A large body of genetic, epidemiological, and clinical evidence, summarized in a 2017 European Atherosclerosis Society consensus statement, causally links LDL cholesterol to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
Kendrick's 2016 review was criticized by the NHS and independent cardiologists for searching only a single literature database and excluding contrary studies.
Multiple national health bodies, including the NHS and British Heart Foundation, reject the claim that statins provide no meaningful cardiovascular benefit.
Kendrick has financial and reputational ties to low-carb/carnivore diet promotion and the pseudoscientific Institute for Natural Healing, a potential conflict of interest.
research_note: Year set to Lundell's 2008 book 'The Great Cholesterol Lie'; the broader cholesterol-skeptic movement (THINCS etc.) predates this but wasn't directly sourced this session.

name: Christ Myth Theory (Astrotheology)
summary: In its conspiratorial 'astrotheology' form, popularized to a mass audience by the 2007 film Zeitgeist and by earlier authors like Kersey Graves and Acharya S, this theory claims Jesus was not a historical figure but a fabricated composite deliberately modeled on earlier solar deities and mythic god-figures such as Horus, Mithra, and Dionysus, with the Gospel narrative encoding astronomical or zodiacal symbolism rather than real events.
evidence_for: Several ancient religions do feature dying-and-rising or solar deities predating Christianity
Some early Christian holidays and iconography were adapted from pre-existing pagan solar and seasonal festivals
A minority, non-astrotheological version of the Christ myth theory retains some support among historians questioning the historicity of Jesus
evidence_against: Most of the specific parallels Zeitgeist claims between Jesus and figures like Horus or Mithra (a December 25 birth, virgin birth, twelve disciples, crucifixion) are not found in the actual ancient source texts and were fabricated or badly misread

The overwhelming majority of historians and Biblical scholars, including secular ones, accept that a historical Jesus existed as an itinerant preacher, even while rejecting supernatural claims about him
The film's main sources, 19th-century amateur mythographers Gerald Massey and Kersey Graves, are considered unreliable and have been discredited by modern Egyptologists and classicists

name: Clinton Uranium One Deal
summary: This theory holds that Hillary Clinton, as Secretary of State, approved a Russian state company's acquisition of the uranium-mining firm Uranium One in exchange for undisclosed donations to the Clinton Foundation, effectively selling US nuclear material access to Russia.
evidence_for: A Russian-linked bank made previously undisclosed donations to the Clinton Foundation around the time of the deal
The deal required sign-off from a State Department Clinton led, among nine federal agencies
evidence_against: The sale was approved unanimously by all nine federal agencies on the review committee, not by Clinton alone
Fox News's own Shepard Smith publicly debunked the scandal narrative on air
No evidence has surfaced that Clinton personally intervened in or was influenced by the donations
Uranium One's uranium was not permitted to be exported from the US under the deal's terms
research_note: Extracted from RationalWiki's 'Hillary Clinton' article ('Foundation' section). Clinton's other associated theories (Clinton Body Count, Pizzagate, vaccine-autism comments) are already atlas entries; Uranium One is the one substantial claim not yet covered.

name: Cloward–Piven Strategy Conspiracy
summary: Conservative commentators allege that a 1966 welfare-reform strategy proposed by academics Richard Cloward and Frances Fox Piven was secretly adopted by Democrats and groups like ACORN to deliberately overwhelm the financial system through bad mortgage lending, engineering the 2008 financial crisis to justify a socialist takeover.
evidence_for: The real 1966 Cloward-Piven article did openly advocate overwhelming welfare rolls to force systemic reform, giving the theory a genuine historical text to point to
ACORN and allied groups did lobby for the Community Reinvestment Act and looser mortgage-lending standards
Some Republican-aligned reports on the financial crisis explicitly blamed CRA and ACORN activity
evidence_against: Most subprime loans that caused the 2008 crisis were issued by non-bank lenders not covered by the CRA at all
The bipartisan Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission found no evidence the CRA or ACORN caused the crisis
Political scientists attribute the 1966 strategy's real-world influence, if any, to unrelated 1970s fiscal pressures, not a coordinated plot four decades later

name: Codex Alimentarius Global Food Control
summary: A health-freedom-movement claim that the Codex Alimentarius, a non-binding UN/WHO food safety guideline compilation, is actually a covert global scheme to ban vitamin/supplement freedom, destroy organic and natural foods, and hand control of the food supply to corporate and government interests.
evidence_for: Codex Alimentarius guidelines do include recommended upper limits for some vitamin/mineral supplement dosages, cited by health-freedom advocates as proof of intent to restrict supplements
Promoted by figures like Alex Jones and the Alliance for Natural Health as part of broader distrust of UN-linked bodies
evidence_against: Codex Alimentarius guidelines are explicitly non-binding on any member country or its institutions
Its stated purpose is standardizing food safety testing and trade, not restricting individual supplement access
No country has cited Codex Alimentarius as legal authority to ban supplements or organic food
research_note: Peaked in health-freedom/Alex Jones circles in the mid-to-late 2000s.

name: Coming Race War
summary: A recurring white-supremacist conspiracy narrative holding that an apocalyptic race war between whites and other racial groups is imminent or secretly being engineered, ranging from Charles Manson's 1969 'Helter Skelter' prophecy of a Black uprising to modern neo-Nazi 'racial holy war' (RaHoWa) accelerationism.
evidence_for: Charles Manson explicitly planned murders in 1969 intended to spark a race war he called Helter Skelter, believing his Family would later rule survivors
Neo-Nazi ideologues (e.g. Ben Klassen) and works like The Turner Diaries have explicitly called for or fictionalized a race war, and have inspired real terrorist attacks
evidence_against: No coordinated 'Black uprising' or organized white-genocide plot has ever materialized despite over a century of such predictions in the US
The theory recycles historical panics (antebellum slave-revolt paranoia, Reconstruction-era 'Black brute' myths, Civil-Rights-era communist-infiltration claims) with no consistent factual basis
Claimed evidence is routinely fabricated or quote-mined (e.g. satirical tweets treated as genuine antifa plans)
research_note: Umbrella entry for the recurring 'imminent race war' narrative distinct from The Great Replacement (which concerns gradual demographic engineering rather than an imminent war).

name: Common Purpose "Shadow Elite" Theory
summary: British fringe activists allege that Common Purpose, a real UK leadership-training charity, is a front for installing ideologically loyal 'graduates' throughout government, media, and public life to advance a hidden pro-EU, globalist political agenda and undermine democracy.
evidence_for: Common Purpose genuinely runs paid leadership courses attended by many UK public-sector officials, creating a real alumni network spanning government and institutions.
evidence_against: No documented evidence shows Common Purpose pursuing any coordinated political agenda beyond standard leadership and networking training.
The claims originate almost entirely with a small number of fringe activists and groups (e.g. the British Constitution Group) without independent corroboration.

name: Creeping Sharia
summary: Popularized by activists like Pamela Geller and Frank Gaffney, this theory claims Muslims are covertly and incrementally imposing sharia law within American courts and institutions, eventually supplanting the U.S. Constitution.
evidence_for: A handful of U.S. civil cases have referenced Islamic religious agreements or arbitration in family-law disputes, as courts sometimes do with any religion's internal agreements
Several U.S. states, including Oklahoma, passed laws explicitly banning courts from considering sharia
evidence_against: References to the Quran in U.S. judicial rulings are rare, while Biblical references are comparatively widespread, without a parallel 'creeping Christianity' panic
Research cited by Frank Gaffney claiming courts were being overrun by sharia cases has been described by legal scholars as methodologically fraudulent
Sharia arbitration bodies operating in the US and UK have no binding legal authority beyond ordinary religious arbitration; civil courts retain final say

name: Washington, D.C. Occult Street Design
summary: A conspiracy theory claiming Freemasons or the Illuminati deliberately designed Washington, D.C.'s street layout to embed occult symbols, most notably an inverted pentagram pointing at the White House, granting dark/demonic forces influence over the US government.
evidence_for: Some D.C. streets, when selectively drawn, can be connected into pentagram- or Masonic-square-like shapes on a map
Several of the city's Founding Father-era planners, including some involved in its design lineage, were Freemasons
evidence_against: An accurate street map shows the cited avenues (Vermont, Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts) do not actually extend far enough to form a five-pointed pentagram pointing at the White House

The city's street plan was principally designed by Pierre Charles L'Enfant on a diamond grid with diagonal state-named avenues, a design pattern that inevitably creates cross- and star-like intersections without deliberate occult intent
The theory requires additional unproven premises that symbols can channel supernatural/demonic power

sources.title: Washington, D.C. street design conspiracy theory — RationalWiki

research_note: Promoted by figures including Alex Jones and David Icke; referenced in mainstream pop culture (Dan Brown's The Lost Symbol).

name: Dinosaur Denialism
summary: A fringe subset of young-earth creationism holds that dinosaurs never existed as prehistoric animals, and that their fossils are either fabricated or misidentified remains, invented by 19th-century scientists as part of a deception to undermine belief in a young Earth and Biblical creation.
evidence_for: Proponents note that the word 'dinosaur' and popular awareness of dinosaurs only date to the 19th century
Argument from incredulity that bones could remain identifiable after tens of millions of years
Claims that the 'dinosaur industry' (museums, media, academia) has financial and ideological motives to keep the narrative alive
Assertion that dinosaurs are absent from the Hebrew Bible
evidence_against: Hundreds of thousands of dinosaur fossils — bones, footprints, coprolites, nests, and even preserved soft tissue — have been documented on every continent
Dinosaur remains were recognized and recorded long before the 19th century, e.g. as Chinese 'oracle bones' and in Native American and ancient Greek traditions
Radiometric dating and stratigraphy consistently place dinosaur fossils in the Mesozoic era, corroborated across independent methods
Several of the most prominent early dinosaur fossil discoverers (Gideon Mantell, William Buckland, Richard Owen) were devout Christians, some explicitly opposed to evolution

name: 2016 DNC Primary Rigging
summary: Leaked internal DNC emails and later admissions by party officials fueled the belief that the Democratic National Committee secretly tilted the 2016 presidential primary in Hillary Clinton's favor despite its official neutrality, angering Bernie Sanders' supporters.
evidence_for: 2016 WikiLeaks release of DNC staff emails discussing ways to undermine the Sanders campaign
Former interim DNC chair Donna Brazile said a joint fundraising agreement gave the Clinton campaign early influence over DNC strategy and staffing
The Sanders campaign said debate scheduling and media coordination favored Clinton
evidence_against: Clinton won a majority of pledged delegates and the popular primary vote outright
DNC neutrality bylaws are internal party rules, not binding law, and staff opinions in leaked emails are not proof primary results were altered
A 2017 lawsuit brought by Sanders donors against the DNC alleging fraud was dismissed by a federal judge

name: 9/11 Hidden in Folded Dollar Bills
summary: A viral pareidolia-based conspiracy theory claiming that folding US dollar bills in specific ways reveals hidden images of the Pentagon and World Trade Center on fire, allegedly proving advance government knowledge of the 9/11 attacks.
evidence_for: Folding certain denominations does produce smoke/building-like shapes from the currency's existing engravings, which spread virally from a 2002 website and were later promoted by Glenn Beck
evidence_against: All US bills above $2 feature an engraved building surrounded by foliage on the reverse; folding shrubbery into 'smoke' shapes works on essentially any such engraving, not a deliberately hidden message
The $100 bill image predates 9/11 by years, undermining any claim of deliberate foreknowledge encoded for that specific event
Similar folding/pareidolia 'hidden message' claims have been made about many unrelated logos and currencies with no substantiated design intent

sources.title: U.S. dollar bill folding tricks — RationalWiki

research_note: A pareidolia sub-theory that circulates within the broader 9/11 truther movement rather than a standalone one.

name: Dulce Base
summary: Dulce Base is an alleged joint human-alien underground facility near Dulce, New Mexico, where reptilian and grey extraterrestrials are said to conduct genetic experiments on abducted humans, with some versions claiming a pitched underground battle once occurred there between aliens and the US military. The legend originated with Paul Bennewitz, an electronics engineer who misinterpreted ordinary nearby military radio traffic as evidence of alien landings.
evidence_for: Alleged testimony from self-described former base employees, published anonymously online
Sandia National Laboratories and Kirtland Air Force Base, both near Dulce, do conduct genuinely classified military research
Persistent local rumors and cattle-mutilation reports in the area predate and fed into Bennewitz's claims
evidence_against: The story's originator, Paul Bennewitz, suffered a documented psychological breakdown linked to his obsessive misreading of ordinary radio signals from Sandia Labs
No photographic, physical, or credible eyewitness evidence for the base has surfaced despite decades of claims
The 'reptilian' and 'grey alien' elements were added and elaborated over time by later, unrelated online authors with no connection to the original account
US Air Force disinformation aimed at Bennewitz, to protect an unrelated classified program he had stumbled near, has been documented as a likely source of some claims

name: ICD-9 E978 "Obamacare Guillotine Executions"
summary: Internet conspiracy claims held that ICD-9 medical billing code E978 ("legal execution"), which lists methods including guillotine beheading, was secretly embedded in the Affordable Care Act ("Obamacare") as proof the US government was preparing mass executions of citizens, often linked to broader FEMA-camp lore.
evidence_for: The ICD-9 code E978 genuinely exists and lists 'legal execution' methods including beheading/decapitation by guillotine, as well as electrocution, hanging, and shooting.
evidence_against: ICD-9 codes are purely descriptive classifications of how a death or injury occurred (for medical records and billing), not authorizations or operational plans for any government action.

The code covers historical and foreign legal executions generally and predates the Affordable Care Act by decades; ICD-10, which Obamacare-era systems transitioned to, does not even retain the E978 designation.

name: Eisenhower Was a Communist Agent
summary: Robert Welch's book 'The Politician' (written mid-1950s, published 1961) claimed President Dwight Eisenhower was a knowing, deliberate agent of a communist conspiracy that also included General George Marshall, alleging Marshall let the Pearl Harbor attack happen and helped the Soviet Union throughout WWII.
evidence_for: Welch, founder of the John Birch Society, asserted he had extensive private evidence but declined to publish it in the book itself
Cites Eisenhower's early-life Democratic Party sympathies as supposedly suspicious for a man later cast as a communist plant regardless of party
evidence_against: The book is internally contradictory, e.g. claiming Eisenhower never declared a party affiliation while also documenting his early Democratic activity
Marshall's actual wartime record (the Marshall Plan) was explicitly designed to stop Soviet/communist expansion in Western Europe
No credible historian has found evidence connecting Eisenhower or Marshall to Soviet intelligence
The claim proved divisive even among conservatives and contributed to William F. Buckley's public split with the John Birch Society
research_note: The same book also repeats the Pearl Harbor advance-knowledge theory (already catalogued as pearl-harbor-foreknowledge); this entry covers its more distinctive claim about Eisenhower himself.

name: Elsagate
summary: A conspiracy theory holding that disturbing, sexually or violently themed videos featuring children's characters (Elsa, Spider-Man, etc.) uploaded en masse to YouTube Kids were a deliberate, coordinated scheme — variously attributed to state actors, pedophile rings, or satanic ritual abuse networks — to desensitize or traffic children, rather than a cynical profit-driven exploitation of YouTube's recommendation algorithm.
evidence_for: A large, sudden wave of nearly identical disturbing 'kids' channels appeared simultaneously in the mid-2010s
Some videos were foreign-language versions, fueling claims of a coordinated international operation
The content's focus on toileting, fear, and mild sexual innuendo aimed at toddlers struck many viewers as inexplicable outside malicious intent
Rapper B.o.B and podcaster Joe Rogan both publicly flagged the phenomenon as 'bizarre'
evidence_against: Investigative reporting (The Verge, 2017) traced the trend to profit-motivated content farms gaming YouTube's recommendation algorithm and keyword-stuffing, not a coordinated psyop
Precursors (Indian 'finger family' DVDs, Tijuana bibles) show the format predates any alleged conspiracy and stems from cheap, high-volume content production
YouTube's 2017–2020 policy crackdowns (channel takedowns, 'made for kids' flagging) targeted algorithm abuse and child-safety comment sections, not a hidden trafficking ring
No law-enforcement investigation has substantiated the pedophilia or satanic-ritual-abuse allegations attached to the phenomenon

name: Executive Order 13603 Slave Labor Powers
summary: This theory holds that Executive Order 13603, signed by President Obama in 2012 to update federal emergency-preparedness authority, secretly grants the president power to conscript private citizens into forced labor and seize private property at will. In reality, the order restates decades-old Defense Production Act authority meant for wartime industrial mobilization and grants no new powers.
evidence_for: The order's text does describe broad government authority over resources, industry, and labor during a declared national emergency
The order remained in effect and was not rescinded by subsequent administrations, including Trump's
evidence_against: The order simply restates authority already granted by the Defense Production Act of 1950, used by every administration since Truman without incident
Fact-checkers such as Snopes found the order grants the president no authority beyond what already existed in law
No instance of the order being invoked for civilian conscription or private property seizure has ever occurred

name: Ethnic-Targeted Bioweapons Programs
summary: The umbrella claim that states secretly develop genetically-targeted bioweapons designed to kill or sterilize specific ethnic groups — e.g. the 1998 Sunday Times "Israeli ethno-bomb" story or claims about apartheid South Africa's Project Coast. No such weapon is known to exist, and geneticists doubt racially-selective pathogens are feasible, though medical bodies have warned about the concept.
evidence_for: Apartheid South Africa's Project Coast did research race-targeted fertility suppression, per testimony to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission
The British Medical Association, ICRC and a US congressional subcommittee have formally warned that genomic advances could enable such weapons
evidence_against: No ethnic bioweapon has ever been demonstrated; human genetic variation within populations exceeds that between them, making clean targeting implausible
The 1998 Sunday Times ethno-bomb story was never corroborated and was widely dismissed
Specific instance claims (HIV, Lyme, COVID as ethnic weapons) have each been independently debunked

name: European Union as the Antichrist's Beast Empire
summary: Christian dispensationalist prophecy believers hold that the European Union is, or will become, the ten-kingdom 'Beast' empire of the Book of Revelation, a revived Roman Empire out of which the Antichrist will rise to rule the world before the End Times.
evidence_for: Popularized from the 1970s by writers like Hal Lindsey, who mapped the Book of Daniel's prophesied 'fourth empire' onto European integration
The EU flag's designer, a devout Catholic, said his inspiration was a Book of Revelation passage about a 'woman clothed with the sun ... and a crown of twelve stars'
The EU's growth from a coal-and-steel pact into a supranational bloc with its own currency and parliament is cited as fitting a 'rising world government' pattern
evidence_against: Numerous historical empires existed between Rome and today, so there is no non-arbitrary reason to treat the EU as the prophesied 'fifth empire'
Prophecy websites promoting the theory openly contradict each other on whether the EU already fulfills the prophecy or merely might in the future
The EU's founding and expansion are driven by ordinary post-WWII economic and political integration, not religious intent

name: Organ Harvesting from Falun Gong Practitioners
summary: This theory holds that the Chinese government has systematically killed imprisoned Falun Gong practitioners, and more broadly other prisoners of conscience, to harvest and sell their organs for transplant, scheduling executions to match organ demand. An independent 2019 tribunal in London concluded the practice occurred 'beyond reasonable doubt.'
evidence_for: China sources organs from recently executed prisoners without clear evidence the prisoners consented
China officially ended the practice of harvesting organs specifically from executed inmates in 2015, implying it occurred before then
An independent 2019 tribunal chaired by a senior human-rights lawyer concluded forced organ harvesting from Falun Gong practitioners had occurred
Wait times for organ transplants in China are anomalously short compared to countries with comparable donor registration rates
evidence_against: The Chinese government denies the practice and states it ended all use of executed-prisoner organs in 2015
Independent, on-the-ground verification of harvesting quotas or targeting of specific religious groups remains difficult given restricted access
Some organizations promoting the claim, such as Falun Gong-linked media, have been accused of conflating separate issues (general prisoner organ use vs. religious targeting)

name: Fort Knox Gold Is Missing
summary: This theory holds that the United States government has secretly sold off, leased, or otherwise depleted the gold reserves held at the Fort Knox Bullion Depository, and that the vault no longer holds anything close to its officially reported holdings.
evidence_for: U.S. gold reserves fell from roughly 20,000 metric tons in the early 1950s to about 8,133 tons by 2013, without full public accounting of the intervening decades
No independent media access to the vaults has been granted since a single 1974 visit
The last full audit including purity testing was reportedly 1953, and the vault was sealed after a 1986 count
Ron Paul and other gold-standard advocates have publicly called for a new independent audit, which has not been granted
evidence_against: The scale of gold at Fort Knox (thousands of tons) would be extremely difficult to remove undetected given its weight and security
Historical gold sales (e.g. Britain's 1999–2002 sale) were public, non-secret transactions, undermining the premise that large sales must be covert
Claims of tungsten-filled fake gold bars shipped to China have been investigated and found unsubstantiated
Treasury officials maintain regular internal inventory checks, even though full independent public audits have lapsed

name: The Franklin Prophecy
summary: A viciously antisemitic speech falsely attributed to Benjamin Franklin, warning that Jews would 'rule and destroy' America unless excluded by the Constitution, was fabricated in 1934 by white-supremacist propagandist William Dudley Pelley and has since circulated as genuine in Nazi, Arab-nationalist, and jihadist propaganda.
evidence_for: The text has been repeatedly cited as authentic by antisemitic and extremist publications for nearly a century, reportedly including by Osama bin Laden in 2002
It purports to originate from the real 1787 Constitutional Convention, giving it a veneer of historical plausibility to the unfamiliar
evidence_against: No record of the speech exists prior to its 1934 publication in Pelley's Silver Legion magazine Liberation
The Franklin Institute has explicitly rejected claims that the original document is held in its archives
The historical Benjamin Franklin is documented as sympathetic to Jews, including donating to Philadelphia's first synagogue

name: Frazzledrip
summary: A QAnon/Pizzagate-adjacent urban legend claiming a secret video exists, allegedly found on Anthony Weiner's laptop, showing Hillary Clinton and aide Huma Abedin sexually assaulting and murdering a child. Believers hold the video is real but permanently hidden because it is 'too illegal' to share.
evidence_for: Widely repeated across QAnon and Pizzagate forums as an established 'fact' with many claimed (but unverified) eyewitnesses
evidence_against: No such video has ever surfaced despite years of claims that it exists
The claim is structured to be unfalsifiable ('real but illegal to show')
Purported screenshots circulated as evidence have been traced to unrelated sources: a restaurant ad, a 1997 death-metal album cover, and an unrelated photo
Cited by a US congressman as an example of dangerous platform-hosted misinformation in a 2018 Google hearing
research_note: Distinct from Pizzagate itself: Pizzagate concerns an alleged trafficking front, Frazzledrip a specific alleged snuff video.

name: "Gender Ideology" Global Plot
summary: The claim, central to the transnational anti-gender movement, that a coordinated global campaign by elites, the UN, academia and NGOs is imposing "gender ideology" on societies to dissolve the family, natural sex differences and national sovereignty. Scholarship traces the term to 1990s Vatican anti-feminist discourse, later adopted by far-right parties across Europe, Latin America and Africa.
evidence_for: Gender-studies programs, international bodies and NGOs do openly advocate for gender-equality and LGBT-rights policies worldwide
Some campaigns (e.g. comprehensive sex-education pushes) are internationally funded and coordinated
evidence_against: Advocacy conducted openly through normal politics and scholarship is not a covert plot; the movement's claims rely on a strawman "ideology" no proponent actually holds
Academic work traces the term's origin to Vatican counter-mobilization against 1990s UN conferences, not to any discovered plan
The supposed conspirators (UN agencies, universities, NGOs) disagree publicly and pursue divergent goals

name: Guerrilla Skepticism Wikipedia Conspiracy
summary: Proponents of paranormal and fringe-science claims, including biologist Rupert Sheldrake, allege that Susan Gerbic's Guerrilla Skepticism on Wikipedia (GSoW) project is part of a coordinated 'ideologue' campaign by organized skeptics to suppress and discredit fringe subjects on Wikipedia.
evidence_for: GSoW is an openly organized, admitted editing project that specifically targets pseudoscience and paranormal articles for skeptical framing
Rupert Sheldrake's Wikipedia biography was substantially rewritten in a less favorable direction during 2013, coinciding with blogger accusations against GSoW
evidence_against: GSoW operates openly under Wikipedia's own editing policies rather than in secret, and its edits are publicly logged and reversible by any editor
Wikipedia edits require sourcing to reliable, published references; framing changes reflect policy compliance rather than a hidden agenda
Mainstream commentary (e.g. The New Republic) concluded Sheldrake's claims of persecution were unfounded

name: GWEN Towers Mind Control
summary: This theory claims that GWEN (Ground Wave Emergency Network), a decommissioned Cold War-era radio relay network built in the 1980s as a nuclear-EMP-resistant backup communications system, is secretly still operating to control the population's minds, alter the weather, or trigger earthquakes, often said to work in tandem with HAARP. In reality only 58 of the planned towers were ever built, the program was abandoned in the early 1990s, and surviving sites were repurposed for GPS relay or sold off as ordinary cell towers.
evidence_for: GWEN towers were a real, if now-defunct, US military radio network
Some repurposed GWEN sites are now ordinary cell towers, feeding confusion between the two
Believers cite real low-frequency 'ground wave' radio propagation science, though it is misapplied to mind-control claims
evidence_against: GWEN transmitters broadcast at only 2,000-3,200 watts, at a frequency (150-175 kHz) far too weak and wrong to affect brain activity
The network was abandoned by the early 1990s due to cost and redundancy with existing communications
No credible physics supports low-frequency ground-wave radio inducing mind control, weather changes, or seismic activity
Photos circulated as 'GWEN towers' are frequently just ordinary modern cell towers

name: Hellstorm (German WWII Genocide Theory)
aliases: Hellstorm: The Real Genocide of Nazi Germany
summary: Promoted by a 2010 book and a 2015 neo-Nazi 'documentary' by white nationalist Kyle Hunt, this theory claims that ethnic Germans, not European Jews, were the true victims of genocide during and after World War II, and that mainstream history suppresses this 'real' genocide to protect the Allied powers' reputation.
evidence_for: Germans did suffer real wartime and postwar hardships, including Allied bombing campaigns, mass postwar expulsions from Eastern Europe, and harsh treatment in some Soviet-run camps
Comparative casualty tables (e.g. German vs. Soviet vs. Polish deaths) are cited by proponents to argue German suffering is understated in popular history
evidence_against: Germany initiated World War II and its population broadly supported the Nazi regime, making comparisons of moral culpability with its victims false-equivalence
Fewer Germans died than several other groups both proportionally and in absolute numbers, and many German deaths were inflicted by the same Nazi regime rather than by Allied action
The film's producer, Kyle Hunt, is an avowed white nationalist whose Renegade Broadcasting outlet promotes other antisemitic conspiracy theories
Mainstream historians reject the 'genocide' framing as a deliberate propaganda inversion, not a suppressed historical fact

name: Hemp Suppression Conspiracy
summary: Popularized by Jack Herer's book The Emperor Wears No Clothes, this theory holds that newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, financier Andrew Mellon, the DuPont Corporation, and drug official Harry Anslinger conspired to criminalize hemp and marijuana in the 1930s to protect Hearst's timber holdings and DuPont's new nylon product from cheaper hemp-based competition.
evidence_for: Hearst did hold vast timber and newsprint interests that could theoretically have been threatened by cheaper hemp paper.
DuPont did patent and commercialize nylon around the same period that hemp cultivation became federally restricted.
Harry Anslinger's Federal Bureau of Narcotics did run sensationalist anti-marijuana media campaigns in the 1930s.
evidence_against: Hemp accounted for well under 2,000 acres of U.S. cultivation in 1937, far too small to meaningfully threaten the timber or paper industries.
Nylon's primary early use was in women's stockings, not the rope, sail, or paper markets hemp would have competed in.
Historians generally attribute 1930s marijuana prohibition primarily to racialized fears linking cannabis use to Mexican immigrants, not industrial sabotage.
No corporate or government documents have surfaced showing coordination between Hearst, DuPont, Mellon, and Anslinger on this specific plan.

name: Rudolf Hess Was Assassinated in Spandau Prison
summary: This theory holds that Rudolf Hess's 1987 death at Spandau Prison, officially ruled a suicide by hanging at age 93, was actually a staged murder by British agents to prevent him from revealing details of a secret WWII-era plot to depose Winston Churchill and negotiate peace with Nazi Germany.
evidence_for: A Freedom-of-Information-released report noted Hess was frail with arthritis and hanged from an anchor point only five feet off the ground, which some found suspicious
Hess's suicide note was reportedly written some 20 years prior to his death
The Soviet government had long blocked Hess's release, and proponents claim Western agents acted once Gorbachev signaled willingness to free him
evidence_against: Death by hanging from a low anchor point via asphyxiation is medically well-documented and does not require a high drop
No physical or documentary evidence of foul play was found at the scene
Hess had already attempted suicide twice earlier in his imprisonment
research_note: Second of two distinct Hess conspiracy claims in the article; assumes (unlike hess-body-double) that the Spandau prisoner genuinely was Hess.

name: Rudolf Hess Was Replaced by a Body Double
summary: This theory, popularized by the 1986 book 'Double Standards: What Really Happened to Rudolf Hess?', claims the man imprisoned at Spandau from 1941 until his death in 1987 was not really Rudolf Hess, but a British-installed double, while the real Hess died around 1942 during a secret peace mission.
evidence_for: A British military surgeon, Hugh Thomas, argued the Spandau prisoner's WWI-era scars did not match Hess's documented wartime injuries
The book's authors linked the substitution to a supposed secret Anglo-German peace negotiation involving the Duke of Kent
evidence_against: A 2019 DNA analysis of a blood sample taken from the Spandau prisoner matched living Hess relatives, confirming his identity
No credible chain of evidence supports a substitution ever having occurred
research_note: One of two distinct Hess conspiracy claims found in the RationalWiki article; see also hess-assassinated. DNA evidence (2019, reported by Smithsonian) definitively refutes this one.

name: Hindu Genocide Conspiracy
summary: Hindu nationalist (Hindutva) rhetoric holds that Hindus face an existential, engineered threat of demographic replacement and cultural destruction from Muslims, Christians, and Western/communist influence, encompassing sub-narratives like 'Love Jihad' and 'Population Jihad.'
evidence_for: The Muslim population growth rate in India has historically exceeded the Hindu rate, giving the demographic-panic narrative a real statistic to point to
Isolated real interfaith marriages and conversions occur and are cited by proponents as anecdotal confirmation
evidence_against: India's 2011 census gap between Hindu and Muslim population numbers was already 800 million and widening, not narrowing
Muslim fertility rates in India fell sharply, from 4.4 to 2.6 children per woman between 1993 and 2020, undercutting the 'replacement' math
At current growth-rate trends, a Hindu-minority India would not occur for roughly 200 years, and only under implausible constant-rate assumptions

name: Homosexual Agenda
summary: The 'homosexual agenda' (or 'gay agenda') is a conspiracy theory, originating with the American Religious Right, alleging that LGBT people are pursuing a coordinated, often secretive campaign to normalize homosexuality, undermine traditional family structures, and indoctrinate children, rather than simply seeking equal civil rights.
evidence_for: Religious Right organizations cite LGBT advocacy groups' public platforms and policy campaigns as evidence of a coordinated strategy
Proponents point to changes in school curricula and media representation of LGBT people as signs of deliberate top-down messaging
evidence_against: LGBT advocacy is open, public civil-rights activism conducted through ordinary political and legal channels, not a secret coordinated plot
No evidence supports claims of centralized coordination aimed at 'destroying' family structures
Mainstream sociological research finds no organized 'agenda' beyond ordinary civil-rights advocacy
research_note: Catalogued to document a long-running, widely-known scapegoating conspiracy theory; scored honestly per the truth rubric (fringe/debunked), genre set to ethnic-religious per brief guidance for hateful/scapegoating theories.

name: Hunter Biden Laptop & Biden Family Corruption
summary: Centered on a MacBook abandoned at a Delaware repair shop in 2019, this theory holds that Hunter Biden's foreign business dealings in Ukraine and China were part of an influence-peddling scheme that personally benefited his father Joe Biden, and that Big Tech, the media, and 51 former intelligence officials suppressed the story ahead of the 2020 election by falsely branding it Russian disinformation.
evidence_for: The Washington Post authenticated roughly 20,000 emails from a copy of the laptop's contents in 2022, confirming Hunter Biden's lucrative board positions with Ukraine's Burisma and China-linked CEFC

Twitter and Facebook did temporarily restrict sharing of the original New York Post story in October 2020, and 51 former intelligence officials signed a letter suggesting the story had the 'hallmarks' of Russian disinformation, which later proved incorrect
Hunter Biden was later convicted on federal gun-purchase charges and pleaded guilty to federal tax charges, confirming some underlying misconduct
evidence_against: Years of Republican-led congressional investigation, including a formal impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden, produced no evidence that Joe Biden received bribes or personally profited from his son's business dealings

The Washington Post's own forensic analysts could not authenticate several hundred thousand additional emails, images, and documents attributed to the laptop, and found evidence some data was added to the copied drive after it left Hunter Biden's possession
The FBI had independently possessed the physical laptop since December 2019, before any of the disputed additional material surfaced

name: Income Tax Denial (Tax Protester Movement)
summary: The tax protester movement holds that the US federal income tax is illegal or inapplicable to most citizens' wages, variously arguing the Sixteenth Amendment was never properly ratified, that the tax code does not actually define wages as taxable income, or that filing and paying is 'voluntary.' Courts have uniformly rejected every version of the argument, and promoters and followers have repeatedly been criminally convicted for tax evasion.
evidence_for: The US tax code is famously long and complex, making it easy to selectively quote provisions out of context
A handful of ambiguous IRS statements about the 'voluntary compliance' system have been misread by protesters as meaning payment itself is optional
evidence_against: The Sixteenth Amendment (1913) explicitly grants Congress power to tax incomes 'from whatever source derived'
Federal courts have rejected every tax-protester legal argument for decades, and the IRS classifies them as frivolous with associated penalties
26 U.S.C. Sections 1, 61, and 63, among others, explicitly define and tax wage income
Prominent promoters, such as Irwin Schiff, and many followers have been criminally convicted and imprisoned for evasion after relying on these arguments

name: Jack the Ripper Royal/Masonic Cover-up
aliases: Jack the Ripper: The Final Solution
summary: Popularized by Stephen Knight's 1976 book 'Jack the Ripper: The Final Solution,' this theory holds that the 1888 Whitechapel murders were committed or covered up by figures connected to the British royal family and Freemasonry, often naming Prince Albert Victor or his physician as the killer to conceal an illegitimate royal marriage and child.
evidence_for: Proponents claim the mutilation of several victims resembles punishments described in Masonic ritual oaths
Prince Albert Victor's secretive private life and rumored secret marriage fed speculation about a cover-up motive
The murders were never officially solved, leaving a vacuum that competing suspect theories have filled for over a century
Prince Albert Victor was a real grandson of Queen Victoria whose private life invited considerable rumor and speculation among contemporaries.
evidence_against: Prince Albert Victor has a documented alibi placing him in Scotland during at least two of the canonical murders
Masonic ritual oaths do not describe the actual wounds inflicted on the victims, and the murdered women had no connection to Freemasonry
No physical or documentary evidence has ever linked the royal family, its physician, or any Masonic lodge to the killings
A widely publicized 2014/2019 DNA 'identification' of an unrelated suspect from a shawl was called 'unpublishable nonsense' by geneticists over serious methodological flaws
Prince Albert Victor has a documented alibi placing him hundreds of miles away in Scotland during at least two of the canonical murders.
The alleged Masonic-ritual mutilation pattern does not match actual Masonic oaths, which prescribe no such punishment, nor the real wound patterns, which varied from victim to victim.
No primary evidence connects any royal or Masonic figure to the murders; the theory rests on speculative books written roughly 80 years after the killings.
research_note: Sourced from the Esperanto-language RationalWiki article 'Ĵakvo la Buĉisto' ('Jack the Ripper'), which covers the same royal/Masonic conspiracy theories as the English-language lore.

name: Jade Helm 15 Takeover Plot
summary: Jade Helm 15 was a real 2015 U.S. military training exercise conducted across Texas and six other states; conspiracy theorists alleged it was secretly a plan to impose martial law, confiscate firearms, and detain dissidents in FEMA-style camps under cover of the drill.
evidence_for: The exercise's unusually large multi-state footprint (1,200 personnel, four military branches) fueled suspicion of a hidden purpose
Nearby Wal-Mart stores that closed for renovation were rumored to be conversion sites for detention/FEMA camps
Texas Governor Greg Abbott ordered the State Guard to monitor the exercise, which theorists took as tacit confirmation of a threat
evidence_against: The Pentagon publicly described Jade Helm 15 as a routine special-operations exercise practicing movement through civilian populations
No martial law, gun confiscation, or detention camps materialized during or after the exercise
Investigative journalists found no connection between the closed Wal-Mart stores and the military exercise

name: Jesuit Conspiracy ("Black Pope" Controls the World)
summary: A recurring anti-Catholic conspiracy theory claiming the Jesuit order's Superior General (nicknamed the "Black Pope") is the true hidden power behind the Papacy and world events, secretly orchestrating wars, assassinations (including Lincoln's), and a New World Order. It draws partly on a forged "Jesuit Oath" of violent extermination against Protestants and heretics, exposed by a U.S. Congressional committee in 1913 as a libelous fabrication.
evidence_for: A purported 'Jesuit Oath' pledging violent extermination of Protestants and heretics has circulated in print since the 19th century
Numerous websites claim the Jesuit Superior General ('Black Pope') secretly controls or deposes popes and shapes world events
Jesuits have historically been implicated in real political intrigues, including the 1605 Gunpowder Plot
evidence_against: A 1913 U.S. House Committee on Elections investigation found the circulated 'oath' was a libelous forgery, originally used to smear a Knights of Columbus member in a Pennsylvania election dispute
No credible evidence supports claims that Jesuit leadership secretly controls the papacy or world governments
The theory conflates the Jesuits' real, separately documented history (e.g., 19th-century ownership of enslaved people to fund Georgetown) with unrelated fabricated claims of secret world control

name: Kosher Tax Conspiracy
summary: An antisemitic conspiracy theory claiming that a hidden surcharge (a 'kosher tax') is added to the price of kosher-certified food, with the proceeds secretly funneled to Jewish organizations or an international Jewish conspiracy. It has periodically resurfaced, including via Quebec politician Louise Mailloux in 2014.
evidence_for: Proponents note that food companies do pay real fees to kosher certification agencies
The claim has been repeated by political figures such as Quebec politician Louise Mailloux in 2014
evidence_against: Documented certification costs are negligible per unit — Kraft reported .0000065 cents per item in 1975
Certification fees pay for the practical costs of inspection and supervision, not any hidden fund
No evidence exists of proceeds being diverted to any political or religious organization beyond certifying bodies' own operating costs
The claim has been widely condemned as an antisemitic conspiracy theory rooted in older blood-libel-style myths
research_note: Cataloguing this hateful theory as documentation, not endorsement; truth scored low per schema guidance for ethnic-religious scapegoating claims.

name: Liberal Media Bias
summary: A widespread belief, especially on the political right, that mainstream news outlets are coordinated or systematically skewed to favor liberal politics and marginalize conservatives, tracing to Spiro Agnew's 1969 attacks on the press and popularized since by figures from Bernard Goldberg to Donald Trump.
evidence_for: Surveys of American journalists have repeatedly found more self-identified Democrats/liberals than Republicans/conservatives in newsrooms
A 2005 UCLA/University of Chicago study (Groseclose and Milyo) claimed to quantify a measurable left-leaning skew across most major outlets
Polling (Gallup, Rasmussen) regularly finds a plurality of Americans believe the news media leans too liberal
evidence_against: Meta-analyses of election coverage (e.g. D'Alessio and Allen) find that partisan bias in U.S. campaign reporting roughly balances out overall
Critics identified serious methodological flaws in how the Groseclose-Milyo study inferred outlet bias from think-tank citation counts
Analysts such as Chomsky and Herman argue corporate ownership, advertiser interests, and profit motive shape coverage more than any individual reporter's politics
Fox News, framed as the corrective to a liberal media, has for years commanded a larger cable-news audience than all competitors combined

name: Lindbergh Baby Kidnapping Conspiracy Theories
summary: Following the 1932 kidnapping and murder of Charles Lindbergh's infant son, and the 1936 execution of Richard Hauptmann for the crime, a range of alternative theories emerged proposing that Hauptmann acted with accomplices, that the ransom money's true owner was never found, or — in more extreme versions — that Lindbergh himself was responsible for his son's death or secretly had him raised abroad.
evidence_for: No fingerprints were found on the ransom note or the ladder used at the crime scene, despite Hauptmann's conviction
Hauptmann consistently denied involvement and claimed the ransom money belonged to his deceased business partner Isidor Fisch
Researchers Gregory Ahlgren ('Crime of the Century') and Robert Zorn ('Cemetery John') have separately argued for alternative culprits or an undetected wider conspiracy
Over 200 people falsely confessed to the crime, illustrating how contested and publicly obsessed-over the case became
evidence_against: Handwriting analysis matched the ransom notes to Hauptmann, and wood from his attic matched the kidnap ladder
Mainstream historians regard Hauptmann's conviction as sound, with alternative theories resting on circumstantial reinterpretation rather than new physical evidence
Claims that Lindbergh secretly had the child raised in Germany or caused his death are not supported by contemporaneous evidence
The 2003 DNA-confirmed discovery of Lindbergh's other secret children (by a German mistress) shows he was capable of concealment, but this has not been shown to extend to the kidnapping case itself

name: LUCIFER Telescope Vatican Alien Conspiracy
summary: Promoted by authors Tom Horn and Cris Putnam, this theory claims the Vatican operates a telescope named LUCIFER on Mount Graham, Arizona to track and prepare for contact with extraterrestrials (or demons), planning to use a coming alien 'disclosure' to unite the world under a Catholic-led New World Order.
evidence_for: The Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope and the Large Binocular Telescope (which hosted an imaging module actually named LUCIFER) are both sited on Mount Graham, and Vatican astronomers have publicly discussed the theological implications of extraterrestrial life
Proponents cite an interview they say shows a Vatican astronomer describing Jesus as connected to a 'star child'
evidence_against: Vatican Observatory astronomer Br. Guy Consolmagno publicly denied making the claims attributed to him and said he knows of 'no credible evidence' of extraterrestrial contact

LUCIFER (later renamed LUCI) is an infrared imaging instrument built for the separately-owned Large Binocular Telescope, an international science consortium unaffiliated with the Vatican; its name is an unrelated acronym/insider joke, not demonology
The Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope (VATT) and the Large Binocular Telescope are two separate facilities with no organizational connection beyond sharing a mountain

name: Lunar Anomalies (Artificial Structures on the Moon)
summary: A cluster of claims, championed by figures like Richard Hoagland and Mike Bara, that low-resolution Apollo-era and Lunar Orbiter photographs show artificial structures on the Moon — towers, domes, a 'castle,' satellite dishes, even a giant humanoid skull — which NASA has covered up. High-resolution modern imagery from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter shows the alleged 'anomalies' are ordinary craters, scanning defects, or photographic artifacts.
evidence_for: Blurry, decades-old Lunar Orbiter and Apollo photographs show apparent geometric shapes some interpret as artificial structures
Proponents Richard Hoagland and Mike Bara published books (Dark Mission, Ancient Aliens on the Moon) cataloguing dozens of alleged anomalies
The claims have been aired repeatedly on the widely syndicated Coast to Coast AM radio program
evidence_against: High-resolution Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imagery covering the entire Moon shows no structures at the claimed locations
Many 'anomalies' have been traced to film-scanning defects, dust, or fluid splatters from the Lunar Orbiter's wet-film development process
The famous lunar 'ziggurat' image was created by two named pranksters in 1999, who later admitted the hoax
Analysis shows a stationary orbit needed for the alleged 'satellite dishes' is physically impossible around a tidally-locked Moon

name: RMS Lusitania Sinking as Deliberate Provocation
summary: This theory holds that the British government knowingly exposed the ocean liner RMS Lusitania to German U-boat attack in 1915 — by withholding a naval escort and shipping war munitions aboard a passenger vessel — in order to draw the still-neutral United States into World War I, and that the wreck was later deliberately depth-charged to destroy incriminating evidence.
evidence_for: A cited 1912 letter from Winston Churchill discusses wanting to 'embroil the United States with Germany' via neutral shipping traffic
The Lusitania was not given a naval escort into the declared war zone around the British Isles despite the known U-boat threat
The ship was carrying small-arms ammunition, which Germany cited as justification for treating it as a legitimate target
Divers have found the wreck shows signs of having been depth-charged and mined some time after the sinking
evidence_against: Orchestrating the precise interception would have required detailed real-time knowledge of U-boat positions that British intelligence did not have at the time
The U.S. did not enter WWI until 1917, two years after the sinking, weakening the 'immediate provocation' framing
The wreck's later depth-charging is better explained by British efforts in World War II to destroy it as a navigational reference point for German submarines
No documentary evidence has surfaced showing the Admiralty specifically withheld protection from the Lusitania as part of a deliberate plan

name: Mars Landing Hoax
summary: An offshoot of Moon-landing denialism, this theory claims NASA's Mars rover and lander missions are entirely or substantially faked, with proponents (often Flat Earthers or Above Top Secret forum members) alleging footage was filmed at Earth analogue test sites like Devon Island rather than on Mars.
evidence_for: NASA and other space agencies genuinely test Mars rover hardware and astronaut procedures at Earth analogue sites such as Devon Island, which visually resembles the Martian surface.
evidence_against: Independent radio tracking by multiple countries' space agencies and amateur astronomers confirms spacecraft signals consistent with actual transit to and operation at Mars.
None of the terrestrial test-site geography (e.g. Devon Island's recognizable landmarks) appears in any actual mission imagery.
Rock and soil chemistry measured by rover instruments is inconsistent with any known Earth location.

name: Med Beds
summary: A QAnon-adjacent belief holds that the military or a hidden elite possesses 'med bed' technology capable of instantly curing any disease, reversing aging, or regenerating lost limbs via 'quantum' science, but suppresses it from the public; some adherents claim the beds have already revived dead public figures.
evidence_for: The claim spread widely through TikTok, Facebook posts, and Reddit communities describing supposed personal experiences
Believers point to real but unrelated military and medical R&D programs as 'proof' such technology could exist
evidence_against: No med bed device has ever been demonstrated, and believers' various described functions are mutually contradictory (cure-all, anti-aging device, alien-contact machine, DNA-changing device)
Companies marketing 'med bed' related products, such as Tesla BioHealing, have been found to sell items containing nothing but cement inside branded canisters costing hundreds of dollars
Freedom-of-information requests to national health services (e.g. Scotland's NHS) confirm no such technology exists or is planned

name: Michael Hastings Assassination Theory
summary: Journalist Michael Hastings — known for reporting that got General Stanley McChrystal fired and for covering NSA/DHS surveillance overreach — died in a fiery single-car crash in Los Angeles on June 18, 2013, one day after emailing colleagues that he believed the FBI was investigating him and that he was working on a big story. Some observers suggest his car was remotely hacked or otherwise sabotaged to silence him, though the LAPD and coroner found no evidence of foul play.
evidence_for: Hastings emailed colleagues hours before his death saying he believed he was under FBI investigation and needed to 'go off the radar for a bit.'
A later Al Jazeera FOIA request confirmed Hastings was in fact under FBI investigation, corroborating what he had said before dying.
The car reportedly burst into flames immediately after impact, with the engine block found a significant distance from the wreck, which some found suspicious.
evidence_against: The LAPD and Los Angeles County coroner both concluded there was no evidence of foul play; the death was ruled an accident.
Friends and colleagues described Hastings as erratic and sleep-deprived, and reportedly using drugs, in the weeks before the crash.
