No cybersecurity researcher has ever publicly demonstrated a working remote-takeover exploit for the specific vehicle model Hastings was driving.
No documentary evidence has linked any government agency to causing the crash itself, as distinct from the separately confirmed, unrelated FBI investigation into Hastings.
research_note: RW frames this as an open conspiracy theory ('no concrete evidence... so they can currently be understood as conspiracy theories') rather than firmly debunking it.

name: Israel/Mossad Orchestrated or Foreknew 9/11 (Dancing Israelis)
summary: A 9/11 truther variant holding that Israel's Mossad orchestrated or had advance knowledge of the September 11 attacks to boost American support for Israel, often citing the arrest of five Israeli men ('the dancing Israelis') seen filming and reportedly celebrating the attacks, and a debunked rumor that thousands of Jews were warned to stay home from the World Trade Center that day.
evidence_for: Five Israeli nationals were detained by the FBI after being seen photographing/celebrating near the attack site and were later deported
Mossad did pass genuine intelligence warnings about a 'major assault' to the CIA/FBI a month before 9/11, including naming some hijackers
evidence_against: The '4,000 Jews warned to stay home' rumor is false; hundreds of Jewish victims died in the towers, proportional to NYC's Jewish population
Mossad's warnings were vague on timing/target and were one of several foreign intelligence tips (including from Algeria and the Philippines) that failed to prevent the attack
The detained Israelis were released after investigation found no attack involvement; their case was unrelated surveillance/visa activity
The theory requires implausible secret coordination to evacuate/protect Jewish New Yorkers while leaving the city's dense Jewish population exposed to toxic dust
research_note: RationalWiki's 'Dancing Israelis' page is a redirect to a section of its 9/11 article; content sourced from that section.

name: 2016 Munich Shooting False Flag
summary: A cluster of fringe blog claims alleging the 2016 Munich mall shooting (carried out by a German-Iranian teenager with a far-right, mass-shooter fixation) was a staged false flag, variously blamed on Mossad-linked journalists, government cover-up, or martial-law preparation.
evidence_for: A German-Israeli journalist (Richard Gutjahr) happened to film both the Nice truck attack and the Munich shooting days apart and briefly uploaded then deleted photos
Early, later-corrected reports of multiple shooters and sirens heard across the city were cited as inconsistencies
Bavarian police initially withheld a firm motive, feeding cover-up suspicions
evidence_against: German police and later investigation found the shooter, an 18-year-old obsessed with mass shootings and Anders Breivik, acted alone with no Islamist or state links
The journalist's dual-city presence is explained by his job as a working reporter, not evidence of foreknowledge
The 'no way to fake it' scale objection: thousands of bystanders and a 2,400-space mall parking lot make a staged event implausible
No credible investigation, journalist, or government body has substantiated the false-flag claims
research_note: Obscure; sourced almost entirely to fringe blogs (aangirfan, nodisinfo, OSNet Daily) rather than mainstream conspiracy communities.

name: Muslim Brotherhood "Civilizational Jihad" Plot
summary: Islamophobic activists cite a 1991 internal memo by Muslim Brotherhood member Mohammed Akram Adlouni, discovered during a 2004 US terrorism-financing trial, as proof of a coordinated, ongoing plan for the Muslim Brotherhood to subvert and destroy Western civilization from within through demographic settlement and institutional infiltration ("civilizational jihad").
evidence_for: The memorandum is an authentic 1991 document that was entered as evidence in the Holy Land Foundation terrorism-financing trial.
evidence_against: The court in the Holy Land Foundation case ruled the memo was not evidence of an actual operational conspiracy and was not relevant to the charges brought against the defendants.

Linguistic and contextual analysis suggests the document expressed the author's aspirational hopes for what the Brotherhood 'should' do, not an adopted plan, and its neologisms show no evidence of having spread within the organization.
There is no evidence the memo was ever seen or acted upon by anyone besides its author until its 2004 discovery.

name: National Sunday Law Conspiracy
aliases: Mark of the Beast Sunday Worship
summary: Originating in 19th-century Seventh-day Adventism, this theory holds that the U.S. government, at the Vatican's secret instigation, is about to pass a national law mandating Sunday worship, fulfilling Biblical End Times prophecy and triggering persecution of Saturday-Sabbath keepers.
evidence_for: Adventist prophet Ellen G. White predicted the scenario in the 19th century in her influential book The Great Controversy, giving the belief religious authority within the church
A real (failed) national Sunday-rest bill was introduced in the U.S. Senate in 1888, which believers treat as a near-miss confirmation
evidence_against: No national Sunday law has been seriously considered by the U.S. Congress in the 130+ years since 1888
Such a law would be flatly unconstitutional under the Establishment Clause and would be struck down by courts immediately
'Vicarius Filii Dei,' the supposed papal title used to derive the number 666, has never actually been an official title of the Pope

name: North American Union
summary: A conspiracy theory, popular among right-wing populists in the mid-2000s, holding that the US, Canada, and Mexico are being secretly merged into a single political and economic union — complete with a shared currency (the 'Amero') and a continent-spanning 'NAFTA Superhighway' — as a stepping stone toward world government.
evidence_for: A real business coalition, NASCO, lobbies for North American trade-corridor infrastructure and published maps of transportation corridors
The Council on Foreign Relations published a 2005 report calling for deeper North American economic and security cooperation
The US, Canada, and Mexico ran a real Security and Prosperity Partnership (SPP) initiative from 2005 to 2009
Kansas City Southern Railway markets a Chicago-to-Mexico City rail line as the 'NAFTA Railway'
A 1999 policy paper by economist Herbert Grubel proposed a North American monetary union and coined the term 'Amero'
Novelty 'Amero' coins were minted and sold as collectibles, which some took as evidence of a currency already in preparation
Talk-radio host Hal Turner promoted images he claimed were genuine Amero currency
evidence_against: The CFR report came from a non-governmental think tank and proposed at most a customs union, not a political merger, and has no bearing on actual policy
The SPP was non-binding and was formally discontinued in 2009 with no successor initiative
No 'Amero' currency exists beyond a 1999 speculative think-tank paper and fan-made mockups
No superhighway project matching the described continent-spanning route has ever been funded or built beyond ordinary existing interstates (I-5, I-35, I-69)
No U.S., Canadian, or Mexican government has ever proposed adopting a common currency or political union
The 'Amero coins' cited as proof were novelty medallions designed by artist Daniel Carr, not government-issued currency
The circulated 'Amero bills' were traced to a Flickr user's political artwork, not real banknotes
A 2007 New York Times investigation found no substantive evidence behind North American Union claims

name: Norway Spiral
summary: A spectacular blue-white spiral light seen over Norway and Sweden on 9 December 2009 was actually a failed Russian Bulava ICBM test launch, but conspiracy theorists proposed it was a dimensional portal, a black hole, a HAARP or Large Hadron Collider effect, part of Project Blue Beam, or (per Richard Hoagland) a secret 'Space Nazi' torsion-field weapon used to intimidate the US into ending human spaceflight.
evidence_for: The spiral's unusual, symmetric appearance was unlike any previously photographed rocket plume seen by the public
Russia did not immediately acknowledge responsibility for the missile test
evidence_against: Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed a failed Bulava missile test from a submarine in the White Sea that night

Near-identical spiral plumes were later photographed from known, non-secret rocket launches (a 2010 Progress launch, a 2011 SpaceX Falcon 9 test), confirming the mechanism is an out-of-control spinning rocket stage venting fuel
Astronomers (e.g. Phil Plait) reproduced the appearance from known rocket-plume physics
research_note: Not previously in the atlas ('spiral' keyword only matched unrelated entries). Impact reflects the mix of proposed mechanisms, from a mundane secret weapons test up to claims of an actual interdimensional portal.

name: November 3rd Seattle Nuclear Attack
summary: A short-lived internet conspiracy theory predicted a false-flag nuclear attack on Seattle, Washington on November 3, 2019, based on 'evidence' drawn from an old Simpsons episode, a Hollywood thriller, a J-pop song, and numerology forums.
evidence_for: Proponents pointed to a 1996 Simpsons episode and the film The Sum of All Fears as supposedly predictive fiction
A gematria-based numerology tool was circulated by fringe outlet Before It's News as 'proof' of the coming date
evidence_against: November 3, 2019 passed with no attack on Seattle or anywhere else
When a fire damaged an unrelated astronomy center in Ankara, Turkey that same day, believers retroactively reinterpreted it as 'confirmation,' illustrating the theory's unfalsifiability
The entire premise rests on fictional media rather than any actual intelligence or leaked plans

name: November 4th Antifa Civil War
summary: A 2017 right-wing media conspiracy theory claiming that Antifa would launch an armed civil war on November 4, 2017 to kill white people, depose Donald Trump, and install authoritarian socialism, based on a peaceful protest day organized by the small group Refuse Fascism.
evidence_for: Refuse Fascism, co-founded by Cornel West and a Revolutionary Communist Party member, did organize and publicize protests for November 4, 2017
A satirical/trolling tweet about 'antifa supersoldiers' beheading white parents was screenshotted and spread as if genuine
evidence_against: Refuse Fascism's own materials explicitly called for nonviolent civil disobedience, not armed conflict
The group had minimal funding and social media following, far short of capability for a claimed nationwide uprising
The 'antifa supersoldiers' quote originated as an acknowledged joke by a satirical Twitter user
November 4, 2017 passed with only the planned peaceful protests; no violence occurred
research_note: Widely covered by mainstream outlets (Snopes, Newsweek, PBS) as a case study in manufactured right-wing media panic.

name: Nuclear Energy Denial
summary: A fringe belief that nuclear weapons and nuclear power do not actually work as described, and that governments and scientists worldwide have fabricated evidence of nuclear technology for undisclosed reasons. It is distinct from the mainstream anti-nuclear movement, which opposes nuclear power on safety grounds without denying the underlying physics.
evidence_for: Proponents cite alleged inconsistencies in photographic and film evidence of nuclear weapons tests
Some point to the secrecy historically surrounding nuclear weapons programs as suspicious
Fringe author Anders Bjorkman's website argues, using his own physics claims, that atomic bombs 'do not work'
evidence_against: Nuclear weapons detonations have been independently measured worldwide via seismographs and atmospheric monitoring
Nuclear power plants generate verifiable electricity across dozens of countries and are subject to international inspection by the IAEA
The physics of nuclear fission and fusion is well established and independently reproduced in laboratories worldwide
Radiation effects from Hiroshima, Nagasaki, and Chernobyl have been extensively medically documented in hundreds of thousands of victims
research_note: Extremely obscure; RationalWiki's own article carries a 'sources needed' tag and cites only a defunct fringe forum and one crank physicist's personal website.

name: Obamacare Death Panels
summary: A claim, popularized by Sarah Palin during the 2009 U.S. health care reform debate, that the Affordable Care Act would create government 'death panels' of unelected bureaucrats empowered to decide which patients — including the elderly and disabled — would be denied life-saving treatment.
evidence_for: Early ACA drafts included optional Medicare reimbursement for voluntary end-of-life counseling sessions, which opponents characterized as a precursor to rationing panels
Universal-coverage systems necessarily involve some form of resource allocation and prioritization decisions
Proponents pointed to anecdotal reports of long wait times in other countries with public health systems as suggestive of rationing
evidence_against: FactCheck.org and other fact-checkers found no provision in the ACA created panels with authority to deny individual patients care based on 'worth'
The end-of-life counseling provision Palin referenced was voluntary and optional, not compulsory or panel-based
Wait-time studies found Massachusetts (which had a similar earlier reform) statistically comparable to other U.S. states without universal coverage
The phrase is widely regarded by health-policy researchers as a scare-tactic neologism rather than a description of any real ACA mechanism

name: One World Religion
summary: Premillennialist Christian conspiracy theorists hold that a global Antichrist figure will forcibly merge all world religions into a single one-world religion during the End Times, engineered by a Masonic New World Order and enforced through the United Nations, persecuting those who refuse to join.
evidence_for: Interfaith ecumenical initiatives and UN-affiliated interreligious dialogue bodies are cited as early steps toward religious unification
Pat Robertson's 1992 book 'The New World Order' popularized the link between a coming Antichrist and global religious/political unification
evidence_against: No unified global religious body with binding authority over the world's religions exists or is close to existing
The world's major religions hold fundamentally incompatible theological claims (monotheism vs. polytheism vs. non-theism) that make forced doctrinal merger implausible
The theory is rooted in a specific, contested interpretation of the Book of Revelation rather than any observed institutional plan
research_note: Distinct from the atlas's existing 'new-world-order' entry (which is about global government/population control); this is specifically the end-times religious-merger variant. Year is approximate, keyed to Pat Robertson's influential 1992 book that popularized the modern conspiratorial framing.

name: Oreo Satanic Templar Logo
summary: An internet conspiracy theory claiming the small cross symbol on Oreo cookies is a hidden Knights Templar/Satanic 'Leviathan Cross' marking, and that the cookie's name secretly encodes Hebrew and Greek words for 'light' pointing to occult meaning.
evidence_for: The symbol on Oreo cookies is a genuine Cross of Lorraine, historically used by the Knights Templar and later adapted by Satanist Anton LaVey as the Leviathan Cross
evidence_against: Nabisco has stated the symbol was chosen because it was understood in Europe as a mark of quality, unrelated to Templar or Satanic symbolism
The 'Or-Eo' Hebrew/Greek 'light' etymology is invented folk wordplay with no documented basis in the cookie's actual naming history
The theory has been traced to a single 2004 Above Top Secret forum post
research_note: Minor internet lore; included for completeness of corporate-logo occult symbolism claims.

name: Orlando Nightclub Shooting False Flag
summary: Following the June 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting in Orlando, Florida that killed 49 people, conspiracy theorist Alex Jones and others claimed the massacre was a 'false flag' operation staged or orchestrated by the government rather than the act of the actual gunman.
evidence_for: Proponents cite the political timing before gun-control debates as suspicious
Some point to inconsistencies in early breaking-news reporting, common to any mass-casualty event, as 'proof' of staging
evidence_against: The shooter, Omar Mateen, was identified, had been tracked by the FBI since 2013, and was killed by police in a real shootout
Extensive victim and witness testimony and physical evidence, plus surviving injured victims, confirm the attack was real
No credible evidence has ever been produced for government orchestration
Alex Jones later contradicted his own false-flag claim by instead blaming the attack on Muslim immigration

name: Oslo/Utøya Attacks False Flag Theories
summary: Following Anders Behring Breivik's July 2011 bombing and shooting attacks in Oslo and on Utøya, various online commentators speculated that the attacks were secretly orchestrated by outside actors — variously blaming Freemasons, Mossad/CIA/NATO, Muslim terror groups, or a domestic cover-up — framing them as a false-flag operation rather than the act of a lone right-wing extremist.
evidence_for: Breivik was a Freemason at the time of the attacks
A Norwegian professor argued attacks of this scale usually have state backing, citing Israel-Norway tensions
Commentators noted the convenient timing of a Muslim group's since-retracted claim of responsibility
Online theorists cited apparent facial-resemblance coincidences between Breivik, Alex Jones, and Julian Assange
evidence_against: Breivik confessed to and was convicted of both attacks, having acted alone
Norwegian police and courts found no evidence of any external sponsor, second perpetrator, or state involvement
The professor who floated Israeli involvement publicly stated he was not accusing Israel of orchestrating the attack
No credible evidence connects Freemasonry, Mossad, or any government to the planning of the attacks

sources.title: Conspiracy theories surrounding the Oslo attacks — RationalWiki

research_note: RW article bundles several distinct blame-narratives (Freemasons, Israel/Mossad, Muslims, domestic cover-up) about one event; catalogued as a single umbrella false-flag entry since they hang together as reactions to the same attack.

name: Pacte de Famine (Famine Pact)
summary: The Pacte de Famine was an 18th-century French conspiracy theory alleging that King Louis XV and grain-trade merchants had secretly conspired to engineer famine and inflate bread prices for profit; spread via pamphlets from 1767 onward, it fueled decades of bread riots and contributed to revolutionary unrest before 1789.
evidence_for: A 1765 grain-trade contract between Louis XV and merchant guild leaders was published and interpreted by pamphleteers as proof of a deliberate scarcity scheme
Recurring droughts, bread shortages, and price spikes through the 1760s-80s lent the theory apparent real-world confirmation, culminating in the 1775 'Guerre des farines' bread riots
evidence_against: Historical scholarship (Cahen, 1926, Revue historique) concludes the 1765 contract was intended to stabilize food supply and prices, not restrict them
No documentary evidence shows the French crown intentionally engineered scarcity
Historians attribute the shortages to poor harvests and pre-industrial agricultural limits, not a deliberate plot
research_note: No English Wikipedia page found for this title (verified via API — missing); omitted wikipedia field accordingly.

name: Polybius (Arcade Game Legend)
summary: An internet urban legend claims that a mysterious arcade game called Polybius briefly appeared in Portland, Oregon in 1981, causing players severe psychological effects, and was secretly a CIA/government mind-control experiment linked to MKUltra. No evidence the game ever existed; researchers have traced the myth to a website created around 2000.
evidence_for: Proponents point to the CIA's real historical MKUltra program as evidence the agency is capable of such an experiment
A handful of early-1980s reports exist of gamers falling ill after extreme marathon sessions on real games such as Asteroids or Berzerk
evidence_against: No contemporary sources, arcade-operator records, or physical cabinets from 1981 have ever surfaced
Investigators have traced the legend's origin to a coinop.org web page created around February 2000, nearly two decades after the claimed events
The purported manufacturer name 'Sinnesloschen' is invented, nonsensical pseudo-German
No verified account of anyone experiencing the described symptoms exists outside the legend itself

name: POW-MIA Left Behind Theory
summary: This theory holds that the Vietnamese government secretly continued holding American prisoners of war after the 1973 Paris Peace Accords and Operation Homecoming, and that the US government covered up their fate rather than negotiate their return. Government investigations, including a 1990s Senate select committee, found no credible evidence any living POWs were retained, though the myth remains commemorated by the widely flown black POW-MIA flag.
evidence_for: Numerous 'live sighting' reports were made by travelers in Southeast Asia through the 1970s-90s
The scale of unaccounted-for MIAs, many killed during secret undisclosed missions in Cambodia and Laos, fed suspicion that records were being concealed
The Nixon administration itself used the POW issue as a public negotiating lever, lending the narrative apparent legitimacy
evidence_against: A 1991-93 US Senate Select Committee investigation found no credible evidence any prisoners were knowingly retained by Vietnam after 1973
Most alleged 'live sightings' could never be substantiated and resembled cryptid-style folklore
Notable claimed cases, such as the subject of the 2013 documentary Unclaimed, were exposed as hoaxes once DNA and fingerprint evidence was checked
Most missing personnel are now understood to have been killed in action, with remains subsequently repatriated after normalization of US-Vietnam relations

name: Protochronism (Romania as Cradle of Civilization)
summary: A Romanian nationalist pseudohistorical movement claiming that Romania (via the ancient Dacians) is the true 'cradle of civilization,' that many world peoples are descended from Romanians, and that many languages derive from Romanian — theories rejected by professional historians and linguists but popular in Romanian nationalist and pop-science media.
evidence_for: Proponents cite selective linguistic parallels between Romanian and various ancient languages
Cherry-picked archaeological finds are presented as evidence of an advanced, globally influential Dacian civilization
The movement has produced numerous popular books, television segments, and documentaries with lay audience appeal
evidence_against: Mainstream Romanian historians, archaeologists and philologists have repeatedly and publicly protested the spread of protochronist claims, including formal letters signed by dozens of academics
Most protochronist 'experts' are professionals in unrelated fields (medicine, engineering) rather than historians or linguists
The core linguistic and archaeological claims rely on cherry-picked data, cognates, and non-sequiturs rejected by comparative linguistics and archaeology
The term itself was coined pejoratively by critics of the movement to describe its methodology

name: Rasputin Assassinated by British Intelligence
summary: This theory holds that Grigori Rasputin's December 1916 assassination was not solely the work of the Russian noble conspirators of popular legend, but that the fatal shot was fired by British Secret Intelligence Service officer Oswald Rayner, based on forensic analysis of the wound and weapon used. It was popularized by historian Andrew Cook's 2004 book and a BBC Timewatch documentary.
evidence_for: The fatal head shot reportedly came from an unjacketed round matching a British Webley revolver, a weapon type almost exclusive to the British Empire at the time
Oswald Rayner was a British intelligence officer stationed in St. Petersburg and personally acquainted with one of the Russian conspirators
Water found in Rasputin's lungs is not conclusive proof of death by drowning, suggesting he may already have been dead when thrown in the river
evidence_against: Contemporary Russian conspirators' own (inconsistent) accounts describe the killing as entirely their own doing, without British involvement
No British government document has ever been declassified confirming an assassination order or operation
Forensic reconstruction of a century-old crime scene from photographs and testimony carries inherent uncertainty
Many historians regard the British-agent theory as a compelling hypothesis rather than an established fact

name: Red Mercury Doomsday Weapon Myth
summary: "Red mercury" is a supposed exotic substance, rumored since the late Cold War to enable dramatically miniaturized nuclear weapons or to have been smuggled out of the collapsing Soviet Union, that numerous black-market scammers have long claimed to sell despite no credible scientific evidence it exists.
evidence_for: Multiple black-market sellers, scam networks, and even an official testifying to South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission have claimed direct knowledge of 'red mercury' transactions tied to a 1987 plane crash.
evidence_against: No verified sample of 'red mercury' with the claimed explosive properties has ever been produced or scientifically confirmed to exist.
A 2015 New York Times investigation concluded it is most likely a hoax used to bait and identify would-be nuclear-material traffickers, or a garbled Cold War code name for an unrelated substance.

No known chemical compound matches the extreme, contradictory properties (both highly energetic and shock-insensitive) that would be needed to eliminate the fission-primary stage of a thermonuclear weapon.

name: Rockefeller Conspiracy Theories
summary: A cluster of conspiracy theories holding that the wealthy and influential Rockefeller family secretly steers world government, global finance, and medicine toward a New World Order via institutions like the Trilateral Commission, Chase Manhattan Bank, and the Federal Reserve — with the family blamed for events ranging from the Kennedy assassination and 9/11 to the Zika virus.
evidence_for: David Rockefeller founded the real Trilateral Commission to promote international economic cooperation among global elites
The family's historical dominance in oil (Standard Oil) and continued influence in banking (Chase Manhattan) and medical philanthropy (Rockefeller Foundation/University) is well documented
In a 2015 interview David Rockefeller light-heartedly confirmed he had 'worked for increased international cooperation all his life,' which theorists cite as tacit confirmation
evidence_against: The Federal Reserve was established by act of Congress in 1913 following a public inquiry, not secret unilateral Rockefeller control

No evidence links the Rockefeller family to the JFK assassination, 9/11, or the Zika virus beyond coincidental institutional ties (e.g., a Rockefeller-funded biobank supplying legitimate researchers with Zika samples)
The Trilateral Commission publishes its membership and reports openly; its stated purpose is conventional policy dialogue, not covert world government

name: Roman Piso Theory (Romans Invented Jesus)
summary: A pseudohistorical claim, originating with Bruno Bauer in 1877 and revived by Joseph Atwill's Caesar's Messiah (2005) and others, that the Gospels and much of the New Testament were fabricated by a conspiracy of Roman aristocrats, often centered on the Piso family, as a social-control tool to pacify Jewish subjects, with the life of Jesus deliberately modeled on the military campaigns of the Roman general Titus Flavius.
evidence_for: Proponents point to claimed thematic and structural 'parallels' between the Gospels and Josephus's Wars of the Jews as their central piece of evidence.
evidence_against: The theory is rejected by mainstream historians, biblical scholars, and even most fringe Jesus-myth proponents as unsupported pareidolia.
Atwill's claimed literary parallels rely on English translations and reportedly do not hold up in the original Greek text.
No independent historical, epigraphic, or manuscript evidence supports Roman authorship of the Gospels or a Piso-family conspiracy.
Classicist and historian Richard Carrier, among others, has published detailed rebuttals showing the theory's claimed parallels are forced and selective.

name: Ruby Ridge Siege Cover-up
summary: Following the fatal 1992 FBI/US Marshals siege of the Weaver family cabin in Idaho, militia and patriot movements came to believe federal agents deliberately entrapped and assassinated Randy Weaver's family, using illegal shoot-on-sight rules of engagement as part of a broader campaign against government critics.
evidence_for: A subsequent Department of Justice review (the Ruff Report) found the FBI's sniper rules of engagement at Ruby Ridge were unconstitutional
An undercover ATF agent had induced Randy Weaver into an illegal firearms sale, later using the resulting charges as leverage to try to recruit him as an informant
The federal government paid the Weaver family a large settlement, widely read as an implicit admission of wrongdoing
evidence_against: Congressional and DOJ investigations found no evidence of a premeditated plot to kill the Weavers, rather negligence and poor command decisions during a chaotic standoff
Randy Weaver was acquitted of the underlying weapons charges apart from failure to appear, undermining any claim the entire prosecution was fabricated from nothing
The 'assassination' framing conflicts with marshals' and FBI accounts that the fatal shootings occurred amid an active exchange of gunfire

name: Satanic Panic (Dungeons & Dragons)
summary: Beginning in the early 1980s, activist Patricia Pulling and her organization BADD (Bothered About Dungeons & Dragons) claimed the fantasy role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons was a gateway to real Satanic worship, occult ritual, and teen suicide.
evidence_for: Pulling's son died by suicide shortly after playing D&D, which she said had 'cursed' his character in the game
BADD pamphlets and Pulling's 1989 book The Devil's Web catalogued dozens of crimes and suicides attributed to the game
Some churches and law-enforcement seminars adopted BADD's material as evidence of a broader satanic-cult threat to children
evidence_against: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control found no causal link between fantasy role-playing games and youth suicide
Sci-fi writer Michael Stackpole's 1990 'Pulling Report' found Pulling's methodology unethical and her claimed professional credentials false
Pulling's estimate of roughly 500 gaming-related suicides a year vastly exceeded the roughly 7 a year actually documented
Both lawsuits Pulling filed over her son's death were dismissed by the courts
research_note: 1980s 'Satanic Panic' moral panic targeting tabletop gaming; distinct from the day-care ritual-abuse panics of the same era.

name: Satanic Ritual Abuse Panic
summary: The Satanic Panic was a moral panic, concentrated in the US and UK from the late 1970s through the 1990s, built on the belief that a vast underground network of Satanists was engaged in systematic ritual child abuse, human sacrifice, and infiltration of daycare centers, the military, and major corporations. Fueled by fraudulent memoirs and coerced testimony, it produced a wave of prosecutions -- such as the McMartin Preschool trial and the West Memphis Three case -- nearly all later overturned or discredited.
evidence_for: Numerous accusers and self-described 'survivors' gave detailed, consistent-sounding testimony under therapy or police questioning
Law enforcement agencies across the US and UK opened investigations and produced training materials based on the claims
A handful of real crimes were initially misattributed to organized Satanic cults, lending the narrative superficial credibility
Numerous individuals came forward, often in therapy, claiming recovered memories of ritual abuse, and several high-profile day-care prosecutions followed.
evidence_against: No physical evidence of an organized Satanic network, ritual sacrifice site, or underground tunnel system has ever been found
Key foundational sources, Mike Warnke's 'The Satan Seller' and Michelle Smith's 'Michelle Remembers', were both exposed as fabrications
Convictions in high-profile cases (McMartin Preschool, West Memphis Three, San Antonio Four) were vacated or overturned after DNA evidence and recanted testimony undermined the prosecutions
Academic consensus classifies the phenomenon as a moral panic driven by coercive interviewing and now-discredited 'recovered memory' therapy
Foundational accounts that launched the panic (e.g. 'Michelle Remembers', 'The Satan Seller', 'Satan's Underground') were later exposed as fabrications by their own authors or investigators.
A 1992 FBI analysis of hundreds of cases found no physical evidence, mass graves, or independent corroboration of any organized multigenerational Satanic abuse network.

Psychologists subsequently determined that many 'recovered memories' of abuse were confabulated or implanted by suggestive therapy techniques rather than genuinely recalled, including physically impossible memories from before age one.

name: Scandinavian Ghost Rockets
summary: In 1946, over a thousand reports of mysterious rocket- or missile-like objects were observed flying over Sweden, Finland, and Norway. Contemporary officials suspected captured German or Soviet weapons tests, but declassified Soviet records reportedly do not support this, leading some ufologists to argue the objects were extraterrestrial craft.
evidence_for: Over 2,000 sightings were recorded by Swedish military authorities in 1946, too many to dismiss as pure hoax or misidentification
Post-Soviet archival research has been cited as failing to confirm Soviet rocket tests as the source
The objects' reported flight characteristics (structured, directed movement) were unlike known contemporary aircraft or missiles
The phenomenon predates the 1947 'flying saucer' craze, making conventional hoax/copycat explanations less straightforward
evidence_against: The most parsimonious mainstream explanations remain captured German V-1/V-2 derived Soviet test flights, meteors, and mass misidentification during a period of high UFO-related anxiety
No physical wreckage or corroborating radar/photographic evidence of an alien craft has ever been produced
Similar 'unexplained aerial phenomena' waves have recurred in many eras and are typically resolved as conventional aircraft, atmospheric phenomena, or hoaxes once records are declassified
'Soviet records don't confirm it' is not equivalent to positive evidence of extraterrestrial origin

name: Secular Humanist Conspiracy
summary: Promoted by evangelical figures such as Tim LaHaye and David Noebel, notably in the 2000 book Mind Siege, this theory holds that 'secular humanism' functions as a coordinated, quasi-religious ideology driving a vast alliance of mainstream institutions -- the UN, universities, the ACLU, major media, and civil-rights and family-planning groups -- toward the deliberate goal of dismantling Christianity and merging the United States into a one-world socialist government.
evidence_for: Self-identified humanist and secular organizations do share broadly overlapping progressive policy goals on issues like reproductive rights and church-state separation
20th-century Humanist Manifestos explicitly articulate a non-theistic worldview intended to influence public life
evidence_against: The dozens of organizations named (NAACP, US State Department, universities, UN, etc.) have no coordinating body and often disagree sharply with one another
Surveys estimate self-identified humanists are a small minority of the population, far too few to secretly run the listed institutions
No internal document or credible whistleblower account has ever demonstrated a coordinated 'humanist' plot
The claim functions primarily as a fundraising and political-mobilization narrative for the religious right rather than a falsifiable historical claim

name: Silent Weapons for Quiet Wars
summary: An anonymous, undated document allegedly recovered from a surplus photocopier claims to be a Bilderberg Group technical manual describing how economics can be modeled and manipulated like an electrical circuit to wage a covert, permanent 'quiet war' on the general public. It was popularized as Chapter 1 of William Cooper's 1991 book 'Behold a Pale Horse'.
evidence_for: The document's dense pseudo-technical language and circuit diagrams are cited by proponents as evidence of insider authorship
It has been continuously reprinted and cited by conspiracy researchers (Alex Jones and others) since the 1990s as proof of elite economic warfare
evidence_against: There is no clear chain of custody for the document and no verification it predates its 1986/1991 publication
A convicted felon, Hartford Van Dyke, confessed in letters to have authored it himself
Its core premise — that socioeconomic behavior obeys literal electrical-circuit physics — is not used or recognized by any economist
research_note: Extracted from RationalWiki's 'Behold a Pale Horse' article (Chapter 1). The book's other chapters (NWO, Majestic 12, Protocols of the Elders of Zion, AIDS-as-bioweapon) all restate theories already in the atlas (new-world-order, majestic-12, protocols-elders-zion, hiv-aids-bioweapon); this is the one distinct claim not already covered.

name: Mysterious Sky Sounds ("The Hum" / Skyquakes)
summary: Beginning with a viral 2012 video from Kyiv, unexplained groaning, humming, and crashing noises reported from the sky worldwide ("skyquakes") have been variously attributed by online communities to HAARP-powered mind control, Project Blue Beam, alien spacecraft, or the apocalyptic trumpets of the Second Coming.
evidence_for: Numerous videos purporting to capture the sounds have circulated globally since 2012, from locations including Canada, the Philippines, and elsewhere.
evidence_against: The original viral video's distinctive metallic groaning sounds were traced to sound effects lifted directly from the 'Transformers' films.
Investigators found many reported sounds are readily explained by mundane industrial noise, construction, underground tunneling, wind, or minor seismic activity distorted by atmospheric conditions.
Many 'copycat' videos claiming the sounds occurred worldwide were confirmed hoaxes made by dubbing the same soundtrack onto unrelated footage.

name: South African White Genocide / Boer Genocide Theory
summary: This theory holds that the wave of violent attacks on South African commercial farmers since the end of apartheid is not ordinary rural crime but a racially targeted campaign — masterminded or tolerated by the South African government, sometimes alleged to be coordinated with international backing — aimed at driving white farmers off the land, with proponents such as Genocide Watch characterizing it as attempted genocide.
evidence_for: A 2002 Genocide Watch report stated over 1,000 white ('ethno-European') farmers had been murdered in South Africa since 1991 and argued this constituted attempted genocide
Some attackers have reportedly made explicitly race-based statements during attacks, such as singling out white victims while sparing mixed-race family members
Farm-attack rates and the brutality reported (including torture) have alarmed farming unions such as Agri SA and the Transvaal Agricultural Union
South Africa has a genuinely high violent crime rate, including farm attacks on white landowners, some with a racial dimension
Inflammatory public statements by South African politicians (e.g. Julius Malema commenting he does not want to kill white people 'for now') are cited by proponents as evidence of intent
The 2025 Trump administration's decision to grant refugee status to white South Africans specifically lent the claim unprecedented official credence
evidence_against: A 2003 study found black, Indian and mixed-race people comprise 48% of farm-attack victims, and white South Africans are statistically underrepresented among murder victims relative to their share of the population and of farmland ownership (73%)

South African police investigations have found no evidence of centralized orchestration; researchers attribute attacks primarily to opportunistic robbery given farmers' rural isolation and perceived wealth
Whites made up only about 1.8% of murder victims nationally in 2009 despite being roughly 8.9% of the population, undercutting claims of ethnically targeted mass killing
Mainstream genocide scholars and South African courts have not recognized farm attacks as a genocide or state-sponsored campaign
A 2025 South African court explicitly ruled that claims of white genocide are 'clearly imagined and not real'
No mass killing campaign has occurred in the two decades since the theory was first articulated, despite repeated predictions of an imminent 'Night of the Long Knives'
The originating 2004 WorldNetDaily article relied on unnamed, unverifiable 'G2B sources' for its central claims

name: Spear of Destiny (Holy Lance Occult Power)
summary: Trevor Ravenscroft's 1973 book 'The Spear of Destiny' claims the Holy Lance (a relic said to have pierced Christ's side at the crucifixion) grants its possessor mystical world-conquering power, that Adolf Hitler started World War II largely to obtain it, and that his downfall (and later General Patton's death) followed from losing it.
evidence_for: Hitler is documented to have had a genuine historical fascination with occult symbolism, and the Vienna Holy Lance was part of the Habsburg imperial regalia he took a personal interest in after the Anschluss.
evidence_against: No documentary or historical evidence supports Ravenscroft's claim that acquiring the lance was a driving motive for World War II.
Historians have identified numerous factual errors and unverifiable claims throughout Ravenscroft's book.
Multiple relics across Europe (Vienna, Rome, Armenia, Krakow) each separately claim to be 'the' authentic Holy Lance, undermining the premise of one unique powerful object.

name: Stab-in-the-Back Legend (Dolchstosslegende)
summary: The stab-in-the-back legend (Dolchstosslegende) is the German nationalist claim, popularized by General Erich Ludendorff and later embraced by the Nazi party, that Germany's undefeated army was betrayed on the home front by Bolsheviks, Weimar politicians, and Jews rather than defeated militarily in World War I. It became foundational Nazi propaganda, was used to delegitimize Germany's new democratic government, and helped justify antisemitic persecution.
evidence_for: Isolated strikes, desertions, and mutinies did occur on the German home front in 1918
Germany's surrender came as a shock to a public that had not been told the true state of military collapse on the Western Front
evidence_against: German military records confirm the Imperial Army was in genuine, terminal collapse by late 1918 due to exhausted reserves, blockade, and the Allied Hundred Days Offensive
Roughly 100,000 German Jews served in WWI and about 12,000 died in action; a 1916 military census intended to prove Jewish disloyalty was suppressed after it instead disproved the premise
Historians uniformly treat the legend as post-hoc political propaganda rather than a documented conspiracy
Similar 'stab-in-the-back' myths recurred after other lost wars (French Algeria, US Vietnam) with equally little evidentiary support, indicating a generic scapegoating pattern

name: Statue of Liberty Masonic/Satanic Symbolism
summary: A conspiracy theory, promoted by figures such as Mark Dice and the site theforbiddenknowledge.com, holds that the Statue of Liberty was secretly designed by French Freemasons to represent Lucifer or to embed Masonic authority into American symbolism, rather than being a straightforward gift commemorating Franco-American friendship.
evidence_for: Sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and engineer Gustave Eiffel were both documented Freemasons
Proponents interpret the statue's radiate crown and raised torch as occult/Masonic iconography rather than classical liberty imagery
evidence_against: Historical records show the statue was a gift from France marking the 1876 centennial of American independence, with no documented Masonic design intent
Mainstream historians attribute the statue's imagery to classical Roman liberty iconography (Libertas), not occult symbolism
The 'Lucifer' interpretation traces to fringe sources rather than any contemporaneous historical evidence
research_note: Year is approximate (Mark Dice-era popularization); RW gives no precise origin date for the claim.

name: Steele Dossier / Trump-Russia Kompromat
summary: A 2016 opposition-research dossier compiled by ex-British intelligence officer Christopher Steele alleged that Russian intelligence had cultivated Donald Trump for years, held blackmail material (including an unverified 'pee tape') on him, and coordinated with his campaign to damage Hillary Clinton's candidacy.
evidence_for: Special Counsel Robert Mueller's investigation documented extensive contacts between Trump associates and Russian nationals and indicted multiple Russian intelligence officers for hacking Democratic emails
Some contacts and meetings described in the dossier were later confirmed by law-enforcement and intelligence officials
Trump campaign figures (Manafort, Papadopoulos, Trump Jr.) were shown to have solicited or welcomed Russian-sourced material on Clinton
evidence_against: The Mueller Report did not establish a criminal conspiracy between the Trump campaign and the Russian government
The 2023 Durham Report found the dossier's primary sub-source's information was largely unverified and may have included Russian disinformation
The most sensational allegation, the 'pee tape,' was never corroborated by any investigation
The dossier was commissioned by the opposition-research firm Fusion GPS, initially for anti-Trump Republican clients and later Democratic ones, a fact used to attack its credibility

name: Stellar Metamorphosis
summary: Promoted almost exclusively by Jeffrey Wolynski via YouTube videos and papers on the non-peer-reviewed viXra preprint server, this fringe hypothesis claims planets are simply old stars that have cooled and lost mass, making the star/planet distinction meaningless. It rejects nuclear fusion, mainstream stellar-formation models, and an evolving universe in favor of an eternally-existing cosmos.
evidence_for: Proponents note that plotting known stellar and planetary masses against radius produces a roughly continuous curve, which they interpret as evidence of an evolutionary continuum rather than two distinct object classes.
evidence_against: The continuous mass-radius relationship is fully explained by known physical density limits, not any evolutionary link between stars and planets.
The hypothesis's claimed mass-loss mechanisms (solar wind, flares, coronal ejections) are many orders of magnitude too weak to convert a star into a planet in any plausible timeframe.
It rejects nuclear fusion despite fusion being directly observed via solar neutrinos and replicated in laboratories.
No peer-reviewed astronomy publication has adopted or tested the hypothesis; it exists solely on viXra (a repository with no peer review) and YouTube.
research_note: No Wikipedia page exists for this hypothesis (verified via Wikipedia API, title returned 'missing').

name: Sydney Siege False Flag
summary: Fringe theorists, including Alex Jones' Infowars, claimed the December 2014 Sydney Lindt Cafe hostage siege was a staged 'false flag' attack orchestrated by government or elite actors to justify expanded police powers and military action against the Islamic State, with the gunman and hostages portrayed as paid actors.
evidence_for: Perpetrator Man Haron Monis had a history of exaggerated and false personal claims, which some cited as evidence he was a scripted 'actor'.
An anti-terror drill had reportedly been held at the same location a year prior, cited by some as 'too coincidental' to be chance.
evidence_against: Monis was a documented, previously known individual with a long criminal record and history of mental illness, not a hired actor.
Two real people, Katrina Dawson and Tori Johnson, died in the siege, independently confirmed by police, media, and a subsequent coronial inquest.
No evidence has ever surfaced connecting the siege to any government or elite plot; the false-flag claims relied purely on speculative YouTube videos.
An official coronial inquest examined the incident in detail and found no evidence supporting a staged-attack theory.

name: Toxoplasma gondii Mind Control / Political Manipulation Theory
summary: Extending genuine scientific findings that the parasite Toxoplasma gondii may subtly influence host behavior, fringe theorists claim the parasite is being used, or exploited by a hidden global elite, to engineer political correctness, pro-immigration attitudes, homosexuality, or general population docility as part of a New World Order agenda. Mainstream science supports only modest statistical associations between latent toxoplasmosis and traits like slowed reaction time or certain psychiatric conditions, not deliberate behavioral programming.
evidence_for: Peer-reviewed studies have found latent T. gondii infection correlates with slower reaction times and higher rates of traffic accidents in infected humans, mirroring behavior-altering effects seen in infected rodents.
A published meta-analysis found statistical associations between T. gondii infection and schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, OCD, and addiction.
Researcher Jaroslav Flegr's toxoplasmosis-personality work won a 2014 Ig Nobel Prize, lending real scientific attention to behavior-altering effects of the parasite.
evidence_against: No study has found T. gondii causes political attitudes, homosexuality, or any form of deliberate mass 'programming'; researchers describe only modest statistical correlations, not causation.
There is no plausible evolutionary or engineered benefit to the parasite from influencing human political views, since its transmission does not depend on political behavior.
The 'gay germ' claim has no supporting clinical evidence and originates from speculative blog posts, not research.
No population-scale mind-control program involving T. gondii has ever been documented; a veterinary vaccine exists only for sheep, unrelated to any human political application.
research_note: Impact scored high (72) because the claimed mechanism is population-wide covert behavioral control, per the schema's 71-90 'mass covert control of populations' band, even though notoriety/truth are low.

name: Transvestigation (Elite Gender Inversion)
summary: A conspiracy theory claiming that a large number of celebrities, politicians, and other public figures — such as Michelle Obama, Brigitte Macron, and numerous historical figures — are secretly transgender, often framed as part of an Illuminati or New World Order 'Elite Gender Inversion' plot, sometimes tied to satanic ritual abuse claims.
evidence_for: Proponents cite digitally altered photographs purporting to show anatomical anomalies in public figures
Adherents perform pseudo-anatomical 'analysis' comparing photographs of subjects to idealized geometric body-ratio templates
The absence of certain private photographs (e.g. of pregnancies) is cited as suspicious by proponents
evidence_against: Multiple flagship images (e.g. of Michelle Obama) have been confirmed by fact-checkers (Lead Stories, PolitiFact, Reuters, AP) to be digitally altered or taken out of context
The core methodology relies on invalid generalizations from average body-ratio statistics, ignoring the wide natural variation in human anatomy — likened by critics to phrenology

A 2022 survey found Americans wildly overestimate the transgender share of the population (guessing ~21% vs. an actual ~1%), a misperception researchers cite as fueling the theory's spread via confirmation bias
No credible evidence has ever substantiated any of its individual claims about specific named public figures

name: USS Liberty Incident Cover-up
summary: During the 1967 Six-Day War, Israeli aircraft and torpedo boats attacked the U.S. Navy signals-intelligence ship USS Liberty in international waters, killing 34 sailors; while official Israeli and U.S. investigations concluded it was a tragic case of mistaken identity, some surviving officers, investigators and researchers believe the attack was deliberate and was subsequently covered up by both governments.
evidence_for: Sustained, repeated attack runs by aircraft and torpedo boats over a lengthy period were called inconsistent with mistaken identity by the Court of Inquiry's senior counsel, Captain Ward Boston
Secretary of State Dean Rusk stated he never believed Israel's explanation and considered the attack outrageous
Captain William McGonagle's Medal of Honor was awarded in an unusually low-key ceremony by the Secretary of the Navy rather than the President, and its citation does not name the attacking nation
evidence_against: Israeli and U.S. Navy Court of Inquiry investigations both formally concluded the attack was accidental, a result of mistaken identity amid the fog of war
Declassified NSA communications intercepts have been cited as supporting the accidental account
Israel formally apologized and paid compensation to victims' families and the U.S. government, consistent with the accident explanation
Israeli aircraft had mistakenly bombed one of their own armored columns the day before, illustrating the level of confusion in the theater

name: Vatican Created Islam, Nazism and Communism Conspiracy
summary: Promoted by self-described ex-priest Alberto Rivera and popularized worldwide through Jack Chick's comic tracts, this theory claims the Vatican secretly created Islam, engineered Nazism and Communism, infiltrates Protestant churches via covert Jesuit agents, and orchestrated the assassinations of JFK and Lincoln, all in pursuit of total world religious and political domination.
evidence_for: Rivera's own detailed first-person narrative, published and defended by Chick Publications since 1979
The claims tap into centuries of pre-existing anti-Catholic and anti-Jesuit conspiracy tradition dating to the Reformation
Millions of Chick tract copies have circulated, embedding the narrative in fundamentalist Protestant subculture for decades
evidence_against: Investigative reporting (Cornerstone Magazine, a Baptist publication) found Rivera fabricated his entire biography: he was never a Catholic priest, never attended the seminary he claimed, and had a documented history of fraud and bad checks
His claimed academic degrees came from a diploma mill, not any seminary
His sister, whom he claimed to have rescued from a convent, was in fact a maid who was never a nun
Historically, the Vatican opposed rather than founded Freemasonry and the Illuminati, directly contradicting a premise the wider anti-Catholic conspiracy tradition relies on

name: War on Christmas
summary: A recurring American culture-war narrative alleges a coordinated secularist (originally framed as Jewish and communist) plot to erase Christmas and Christianity from public life, with roots in a 1959 John Birch Society pamphlet, revived as an annual media phenomenon by Fox News host Bill O'Reilly from 2004 onward.
evidence_for: The John Birch Society's 1959 pamphlet 'There Goes Christmas' explicitly alleged a communist plot to remove Christ from Christmas
Some retailers and institutions have shifted toward inclusive 'Happy Holidays' greetings and generic seasonal displays, which proponents cite as evidence of the trend
Earlier antisemitic tracts, including Henry Ford's The International Jew, made similar 'war on Christmas' claims decades before the modern version
evidence_against: The proportion of American Christians who say Christmas has religious meaning to them has been increasing, not decreasing, even as church membership generally declines
Many popular 20th-century Christmas songs were written by Jewish songwriters, undermining the claim of a Jewish plot to secularize the holiday
Fox News host Bill O'Reilly's own website was found to sell 'holiday' (not 'Christmas') ornaments during his on-air campaign against the practice

name: Paul Wellstone Assassination Theory
summary: Following the fatal October 2002 plane crash that killed US Senator Paul Wellstone eleven days before his re-election, some conspiracy theorists alleged he was assassinated — often blaming the Bush administration or Dick Cheney — in retaliation for his vote against authorizing the Iraq War.
evidence_for: Wellstone was one of very few US senators to vote against authorizing the Iraq War, both in 1991 and 2002, and his death came at a politically consequential moment shortly before a close re-election race.
evidence_against: The National Transportation Safety Board investigation attributed the crash solely to pilot error in poor weather conditions, finding no evidence of mechanical sabotage or foul play.
No physical, testimonial, or documentary evidence has ever linked any government official or political operative to the crash.

name: WHO-IAEA Conspiracy
summary: A conspiracy theory, promoted mainly by anti-nuclear activist groups, alleging that a real 1959 cooperation agreement between the World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) secretly gives the IAEA veto power over WHO research on radiation health effects, explaining why WHO reports on incidents like Chernobyl describe comparatively minor health impacts.
evidence_for: A real 1959 WHO-IAEA cooperation agreement exists and is cited as the theory's textual basis
Activist group Independent WHO and several anti-nuclear organizations have campaigned publicly on the claim for years
Physician and anti-nuclear campaigner Helen Caldicott has endorsed the theory
evidence_against: The full text of the 1959 agreement explicitly preserves WHO's independent right to pursue health research 'without prejudice,' contrary to claims of IAEA veto power
The WHO has issued a public statement explicitly denying it is subordinate to the IAEA on health matters
The lead promoter group (Independent WHO) also promotes unrelated pseudoscientific claims, such as apple pectin removing radionuclides from the body, undermining its credibility

name: Whole Language Reading Conspiracy
summary: Some religious-right figures, including Phyllis Schlafly and the John Birch Society, claimed that the 'whole language' ('look-say') method of teaching reading was deliberately promoted by liberal educators to instill moral relativism and undermine belief in objective truth in American schoolchildren, rather than being a legitimate (if contested) pedagogical approach.
evidence_for: Whole language's resurgence in the late 1980s-1990s coincided with a push to add multiculturalism to school curricula, which proponents read as connected
Phyllis Schlafly authored phonics-instruction books (e.g. 'Turbo Reader') explicitly framing the debate in these terms
evidence_against: The phonics-vs-whole-language debate is a mainstream, decades-old pedagogical dispute among reading researchers with no documented ideological conspiracy behind either approach
Whole language and phonics methods have each cycled in and out of favor multiple times since the 1800s for unrelated historical reasons (post-Sputnik math/science pushes, etc.)
No organizational documentation has ever surfaced showing a coordinated plot to use reading instruction for ideological indoctrination
research_note: Niche, low-notoriety claim confined mostly to religious-right homeschooling circles; included per brief since it is a distinct, RationalWiki-cataloged conspiracy theory not present elsewhere in the atlas.

name: Murder of Lee Rigby False Flag Theory
summary: Following the 2013 murder of British soldier Lee Rigby by two Islamist extremists in Woolwich, London, some conspiracy theorists — including an Islamic student group alleging Masonic involvement — claimed the attack was a staged 'false flag' operation, citing an allegedly bloodless second video of the attacker's post-attack speech.
evidence_for: A second circulating video of the attacker's speech appeared to show his hands without visible blood
Some claimed the described beheading attempt was inconsistent with the amount of blood visible at the scene
The attacker's reference to 'our lands' despite a London accent struck some as scripted or incongruous
evidence_against: The 'bloodless hands' video was shown to be the result of a simple color-grading/compression alteration affecting all red tones in the footage, not evidence of staging
Early reports of a full beheading were later corrected to an attempted beheading, resolving the blood-quantity objection
The attacker's phrase 'our lands' is readily explained as referring to Muslim-majority countries rather than his literal birthplace
Both perpetrators were convicted based on extensive video, forensic, and eyewitness evidence, with the attack widely documented by uninvolved bystanders

name: Yuri Gagarin Death Conspiracy
summary: Because the Soviet government kept the 1968 death of cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin in a jet crash officially unexplained for over three decades (records were declassified only in 2003), theories arose claiming he was assassinated by a jealous Leonid Brezhnev, faked his own death, or was abducted by aliens. The declassified KGB investigation attributes the crash to bad weather information combined with a bird strike or a sudden evasive maneuver.
evidence_for: The Soviet government withheld official crash details for over three decades, fueling suspicion
Gagarin's fame and political value made him a plausible target for rivalry within the Soviet hierarchy
Multiple competing 'official' explanations circulated over the years before declassification
evidence_against: The 2003 declassified KGB report attributes the crash to bad weather data and a bird strike or evasive maneuver around a second aircraft
No physical or testimonial evidence supports assassination, staged-death, or alien-abduction claims
The decades of secrecy are well explained by ordinary Soviet-era institutional opacity around any embarrassing incident, not a specific cover-up

name: Zeeman Crater Alien Base
summary: Promoted primarily by Richard C. Hoagland, this theory holds that 1994 Clementine probe imagery of the Moon's far-side Zeeman crater reveals extraterrestrial structures and technology, and that the U.S. government has concealed this discovery, allegedly encoding clues to the cover-up in the mission's logo patch.
evidence_for: Hoagland and followers interpret certain shapes in Clementine probe photos of Zeeman crater as artificial structures resembling scales or domed ruins
The Clementine mission patch is claimed to contain hidden symbolic references to the cover-up
Some ufologists cite an anomalous massif on the crater's rim as evidence of non-natural origin
evidence_against: The alleged 'artificial structures' are consistent with ordinary lunar regolith and rock formations (pareidolia)
Planetary geologists attribute the anomalous rim massif to unusual impact dynamics rather than artificial construction
No peer-reviewed lunar science has found evidence of structures at Zeeman crater
Hoagland has a documented history of misinterpreting NASA imagery, e.g. the 'Face on Mars'
